review:
this game is legitimately one of the most frustrating competitive games i have played, and it is purely about the performance of the game
i remember going out of my way to install blurred backgrounds and having to do rather low-level things that a normal user / player should not have to deal with, such as add specific launch commands , messing with quite a few game files and installing additional third party software just to be able to extract as much performance out of this mess of an unoptimized game this is
my machine is significantly more than capable to run this, and was, even before i upgraded my hardware.
even when i was around plat when i had been playing this game competitively for a long time, i managed to push down my distaste and managed to grow around how awful playing the game felt due to latency (despite my connection being perfect, even better now, again due to the upgrades of my parts / peripherals over time) and general handling, but to come back after a long time and see that absolutely nothing has changed, and potentially has gotten even worse, is vehemently aggravating, more than i can verbalise
this can be a fun game to play casually with your friends, but trying to get into playing it competitively can and most likely will make you do things in order to compensate for the fault of the game engine

review:
This game has been my personality for the past 3 years. I have hit diamond fairly consistently and each season I question why Im still playing. This review is not to dog on the game itself (for the most part) but rather the direction its going as a seasoned player.
vvvvvvvv

BMG is a company that seems to focus on all the wrong things, one of which being the shittiest tiktok/instagram reels ive seen since Chips Ahoy made animated advertisements. Another being crossovers that now cost roughly $20 a single skin, thats 20 whole USA dollars for a 2d Funko Pop, at that point, just install mods brother. I understand its a free game and bills need to be made but we don't get anything in return for giving more money. Tournaments are funded less and less and the most exciting thing they've added has been asking you if you prefer sweet or sour (I wish I was exaggerating). 

The game itself is awesome and has been my favorite fighting game for years, but it feels like BMG has lost its innovation for Brawlhalla. There is sincerely nothing to pursue in this game other than rank. Which is ironic because if you don't have the software requirements you will never hit the rank of your dreams, requirements you need for a game that looks like it runs off of Flash. The community itself is also the most toxic dumpster fire I've ever witnessed for a video game. If you are a new player wanting to just have a fun on your day off, good luck. If you are a seasoned player trying to come back to something fresh and new, good luck. If you are getting a hang of the game and want to pursue ranked without someone telling you to end your life whether you win OR lose, good luck.

And please BMG for the love of god stop making reels, its agonizing. Other than that - 7/10 for the game itself. xoxo

Rating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️✨ (6.5/10)

Brawlhalla is a free and accessible fighting game that offers fast and chaotic combat in the style of Super Smash Bros., but with its own approach. It is ideal for casual matches with friends or for those looking for a light alternative to the combat platform genre.

With a huge roster of characters, including crossovers with popular franchises, Brawlhalla bets on variety and visual spectacle. The mechanics are easy to learn, and that makes it a good gateway for new players. In addition, its availability on multiple platforms with crossplay is a big plus.

The competitive mode exists, but its ranking and matchmaking system leaves something to be desired compared to other more polished fighters. The experience is sometimes affected by lag or disconnections, and although it has an active base, the game fails to maintain the same level of refinement in the competitive scene.

📉 Added to that, its monetization model with rotation of characters and cosmetics can be frustrating for those looking for a more complete experience without spending money.

🎯 Conclusion:
Brawlhalla is a fun and light game, ideal for casual sessions and online parties, but it falls short in depth and balance for the most demanding of the genre. It has potential, but it is noticeable that it prioritizes accessibility over complexity.

A good pastime, but not an unforgettable fighting title.

review:
Brawlhalla is what happens when you mix Smash Bros.-style combat with a free-to-play model that actually works. With over 50 legends, cross-platform play, and fast-paced brawling, it’s one of the best F2P fighting games out there. But is it for everyone?

The Good:
✅ Tons of Characters & Crossovers: From Rayman to WWE superstars, the roster keeps growing.
✅ Easy to Learn, Hard to Master: Simple controls but deep mechanics make it great for casuals and pros alike.
✅ Frequent Updates: New legends, skins, and balance patches keep things fresh.
✅ Cross-Platform & Stable Netcode: Play with friends on any platform with smooth online matches.

The Bad:
❌ Monetization Can Be Annoying: While the game is free, unlocking legends without spending money takes time.
❌ Floaty Combat Feel: Some players might not enjoy the aerial-heavy movement style.
❌ Matchmaking Can Be Hit or Miss: Ranked can sometimes feel unbalanced, especially for new players.

Final 
Brawlhalla is one of the best free-to-play fighters around, offering fun combat and a growing community. While it may not replace Smash Bros., it holds its own as a fantastic alternative for PC and consoles.

⭐ 8/10 – FREE, fun, and surprisingly deep!

review:
I have never played a game so fucking dogshit at doing its own gameplay/mechanical features.
Theres such a unequal distribution of damage/power amongst the characters, where one character will miss their sig at point blank while another can hit you from across the map (especially with the newer legends being released). Theres been an absolute **0** meaningful balance changes done to any character since the game's release, the input registration is completely AWFUL (for me at least) where I cant even get my movement down because it feels like im playing on 200 ping when im playing on my home servers. And to top it all off, the community is always fallen on deaf ears because the developers dont seem to have any. They wont even respond to support emails. I mean really? name 1 fucking game where you had to actively try and look for a fix to the terrible input delay and come up empty handed. The only content update there has been are skin releases. fucking skin releases. If they put as much effort into bettering the game then they would into their shitty skins, then more people would put their money toward a GOOD GAME. Complete pile of shit, dont waste your time with this game.

review:
I love Brawlhalla. I've been playing for 5 years, and I have made some great memories thanks to this game. However, nothing makes me madder than playing this game. Brawlhalla is the single most frustrating experience anyone can ever have in any fighting game. As a casual game it is an incredibly fun experience even if it has it issues like a lack of a casual 1v1 queue and a steep learning curve, but as a competitive game its down-right horrible. High-level game play boils down to who can bait out an attack first so they can punish. This results in almost every pro level match looking like a tap dancing competition. Not only is this not fun to play against, its not fun to watch at all. The only thing that keeps people going back to the tournament streams is the hope that its not a passive fest this time, and whatever old skins and new colors you can get by watching them. Talking about skins, crossovers have been getting way too expensive recently. People spend upwards of $30 dollars on ONE skin. Yeah ONE skin only. Not only are they expensive, they harm game-play since it makes it confusing which legend you're fighting, and can lead to losses because you're opponent doesn't know who they are fighting. And for the love of god, can some older less popular legends please get buffed. The game has more than 60 playable characters, so why when I hop on the game I see the same 5 legends, Koji, Teros, Mordex, Nix, and Val on the game. review: Brawlhalla is a platformer fighter that does take some inspiration from SSB (Super Smash Bros) but has very unique twist. One of them being unique weapons and unique stats making every character different from one another. They also have different modes like Ranked and just "Play" which is a bit more fun and casual. Yes this game is free to play which means it has a battle pass and premium currency, but you can still get legends with gold by just playing the game. Brawlhalla as has a feature where you can watch videos and every 10 views gets you different cosmetics or just more coins. The only downside to this is that it has a cool down which means you have to wait an amount of time before watching more videos, but the best thing about this is every 50 views it gets you a grand chest! This contains the one thing that everyone wants but is locked behind a paywall... legend skins! Now you can get legend skins from every 50 views but that takes time and you are not guaranteed to get skins. One mistake I had is that there are weekly legends and when you first play the game you better choose one and learn the character a little and start earning gold because if you want to fully unlock the character you need 5400 gold on average (some are lower) for the character. I had taken a liking to a character and one day it was swapped out of weekly rotation, this made me stop playing the game which I regret because it is so fun. Highly recommend! (I have not made a purchase on this game nor gotten any paid things for free)

I like the cosmetics that come from battlepasses but does a fighting game really need one especially if you cant get the next battlepass with the coins received (its locked behind a money only paywall) and a single skin costing 6 bucks is just plain dumb for how little you actually get and that's not even mentioning that colab skins are going up in price more and more (there is more issues i have but basically most cosmetics aren't worth it). I will end it with this i thinks brawl is one of the better fighing games out there but the community is full of awful people and the monetization is getting out of hand but i think it is worth playing if you like smash bros types of fighting games but want something less clunky (ps if you arent enjoying it try getting high it helped me)

Review: Brawlhalla

Brawlhalla, as a free-to-play fighting game, has managed to maintain a relatively consistent and sizable community for years. In the following review, I want to share my thoughts on why that might be the case.

Gameplay:

Unlike other games in the genre, such as Mortal Kombat, Street Fighter, or Injustice, Brawlhalla features a much simpler combat system. There are light and heavy attacks, each of which depends on the character you’re playing, the weapons they are using, and the direction in which the attack is executed.
For example, a side attack with blasters has a different range, hitbox position, and speed than an side attack with a greatsword.

This means that each legend plays completely differently. However, with light attacks, combos can be performed that, depending on the stats, can also be executed by other legends if they are using the same weapons. This creates a sweet spot in the category of "easy to learn, hard to master," making the game accessible to a large audience.

Story:

Brawlhalla doesn’t have a traditional story, but you can read through various entries to learn more about the lore of the characters.

Graphics:

The game features an art style that gives it a relatively timeless visual appeal. I find it simple yet beautifully designed.

Conclusion:

Brawlhalla is a fighting game that, by being free-to-play and easy to learn, continues to attract a large number of players even today. It convinces with a blend of simplicity and a touch of complexity.

Personally, even after several years, I still enjoy jumping into a few matches of Brawlhalla or even ranked mode from time to time. If what I’ve described sounds interesting to you, I highly recommend giving it a try.

That’s it for this review. See you in the Brawl. Until then!

Saderhorn

review:
Overall a very well made game with a good system, simple and easy to understand gameplay, fortunately or unfortunately it has become a very competitive game over time, but it always pleases new players who are learning, the only negative point would be the amount of anger you get in this game, but apart from that it is a great game.
a caveat for the game's anti-cheat which is very light and runs smoothly (at least until the date of posting this review)

В целом, очень хорошо сделанная игра с хорошей системой, простым и понятным геймплеем, к счастью или к сожалению, со временем она стала очень конкурентоспособной игрой, но она всегда радует новых игроков, которые учатся, единственным отрицательным моментом будет количество гнева, которое вы получаете в этой игре, но в остальном это отличная игра.
предостережение по поводу античита игры, который очень легкий и работает гладко (по крайней мере, до даты публикации этого обзора)

review:
Ah, Brawlhalla—a veritable ballet of digital destruction, a symphony of steel and sorcery, a grand coliseum where pixelated warriors clash in an eternal tempest of skill and chaos! To call this mere “game” would be an insult of the highest order; nay, it is a testament to the boundless ingenuity of humankind’s foray into the realm of electronic gladiatorial combat.

Gameplay – A Dance of the Divine (10/10)
The very act of engaging in Brawlhalla’s combat is akin to partaking in a celestial waltz—each strike, each dodge, each weapon toss a perfectly choreographed note in the opera of battle. One does not simply "fight" in Brawlhalla; one ascends beyond mortal comprehension, grasping the esoteric artistry of aerial movement and edge-guarding with a reverence reserved only for the finest of martial philosophies.

Characters – A Pantheon of Unparalleled Valor (9/10)
The warriors of Brawlhalla, known as Legends, are a collection so vast and varied that one might suspect the gods themselves curated them from the annals of myth and history. From valiant knights to intergalactic bounty hunters, each Legend wields their weapons with a finesse that would make even the most seasoned warriors weep tears of admiration. And let us not forget the crossovers—why, where else may one witness the ungodly spectacle of Finn the Human battling Ezio Auditore in an aerial duel of destiny?

Graphics – A Feast for the Retinal Orbs (8/10)
The art style is nothing short of a visual serenade—a colorful, whimsical aesthetic that masks the true brutality lurking beneath. Every map, every explosion, every perfectly timed ground-pound is rendered in an animated splendor that does not seek to overwhelm but instead beckons the eye with a playful invitation to destruction.

Soundtrack – A Symphony of Smashing (8/10)
The music, while often overlooked, provides a gallant backdrop to the carnage. It is neither intrusive nor lackluster, but rather a noble accompaniment to the havoc unfolding upon the screen. A melody to which one shall undoubtedly lose many a battle but do so with the grandeur befitting a fallen champion.

Final Verdict – A Game Worthy of the Digital Pantheon (9/10)
To play Brawlhalla is to enter an arena where only the most cunning, the most dexterous, and the most gloriously unhinged shall prevail. It is an experience both exhilarating and humbling, a reminder that in the grand stage of digital combat, one’s triumphs are fleeting, but the pursuit of mastery is eternal.

Would I recommend this exquisite title? Verily, with the force of a thousand Thor hammers. Download it, embrace the chaos, and prepare thyself for a journey of unparalleled spectacle.

review:
Brawlhalla is just one of those classic brawler games where you can really sit down with a few buddies and have at it for a couple hours. Gameplay gets a little old quickly so it's also one of those games you come back to every now and then rather than play every day, in my opinion. 

Now here's where it goes bad for me, the online community of this game is absolutely next level gamers. I just don't have the will to sit and watch YouTube tutorials on how to do the longest combo on all of the characters and meta game as hard as is required to do well online. 

It really feels like knowing there is a blender on the other side of the door you're about to enter while also knowing that someone much larger, smarter, more technically skilled, and faster than you is waiting to grab you and throw you in it as soon as you open said door. There's just no way to avoid it in every single match you play

Overall, I'd only recommend this game for the local multiplayer or playing with buddies online, otherwise, it would be more fun to juggle lava rocks than just got spit out of an active volcano and directly into the palms of your hands

review: Used to love this game, but once you get an elo past 1500, you will realise how many S botters and script runners there are playing. There's tons of videos showing people hacking on youtube, yet the devs refuse to acknowledge this fact. I've reported people for speed hacking, breaking every attack that cant be broken with the moves they use, dodging every attack thats dished out, including after they hitbox with damage sound. Before you try to tell me it's lag, brawlhalla doesnt work that way, if you have lag so does your opponent. After their last update punishing the character weapon types that least often use hacks, scripts and exploits, and buffing 2 of the most often used weapons for S botters, they've made it almost impossible to beat the hackers like I was often able to before, and before you go screaming about me having a "skill issue" I rank in the top 10% of global rankings, I'm consistently able to beat people who are clearly  cheating, it's easy to tell because they often use the same handful of characters, and have the exact same play styles and boosted players stats that are beyond what the game will allow. I've been holding off writting this review because this was my go to fighting game, but as it stands after nerfing the greatsword(what I most often use to win against people who cheat, including youtube accounts who record themselves doing so, and have known steam names) I simply cant recommend this game. If they would admit cheating is easy, and a HUGE amount of people can be seen doing it, and how huge the demand for these hack programs is. . .(check youtube comment sections for S bot.) Then maybe I would consider recommending this. Instead, I will be uninstalling. If you suck at this game, it's worth playing, you wont run into almost any cheaters, but once you get good enough to go gold and up, at LEAST 25% of the matches you have will be played against S bot. Broken, hot pile of absolute garbage. Wish I didnt have to write this, wish it was different, oh well. . .guess I'll go play Mortal Kombat against hackers, at least that will be more entertaining, and everyone knows they're there and admit it.

review:
Brawlhalla is a fast-paced, fun, and highly competitive platform fighter that I’ve been playing for a long time. With a huge roster of characters, cross-platform play, and frequent updates, it’s one of the best free-to-play fighting games available. The gameplay is easy to pick up but hard to master, making it accessible for casual players while still offering deep mechanics for those who want to compete seriously.

One of Brawlhalla’s biggest strengths is its variety, different weapons, legends, and game modes keep things fresh. The movement and combat feel smooth, and every match is a mix of skill, strategy, and fast reactions. However, the game does have balance issues at times, and some mechanics (like dodge reads and certain weapon metas) can feel frustrating.

Despite that, Brawlhalla remains a solid fighting game that doesn’t rely on pay-to-win mechanics, every legend can be unlocked through gameplay. Whether you’re playing casually with friends or grinding ranked matches, it’s a game that keeps pulling you back in. If you enjoy platform fighters, this is one you should definitely try

review:
I enjoy the gameplay itself—it's really entertaining. And that's about it.
Ranked and casual matches are an absolute nightmare, mainly because of the player base and the ridiculous stat system. The game is full of toxic players, many of whom just spam heavy attacks or refuse to let you grab a weapon. On top of that, most of them play characters with both high defense and high damage, making the experience incredibly frustrating and unfair.
Now, I don’t claim to be amazing at the game, but with 400 hours and a 1700 Elo rating, I have a solid understanding of how it works. And honestly, it’s a mess. There are completely unbalanced weapons that allow for near-infinite combos if the opponent makes a single mistake in dodging. Typically, if you miss a heavy attack, you should be open to punishment, right? Well, a lot of the newer legends don’t follow that logic at all. Many of them have heavy attacks that are almost unpunishable, making them absurdly forgiving to play against.
Take Imugi, for example—he’s an absolute tank with some of the highest attack and defense stats in the game. He can just spam his ridiculous attacks with little to no consequence. That’s not skill; that’s just abusing an overpowered character. How is that fair? If two players of equal skill face off, the one using a broken legend will almost always win.
I just played against a Xull who was absolute garbage. He spent the entire match standing at the edge of the stage, waiting to spam attacks. I still managed to beat him, but the fact that he had the same Elo as me was absurd. I genuinely thought he was still in his placement matches, but no—he was already ranked at my level. That kind of Elo inflation makes games a complete pain because you constantly run into players who are clearly worse than you but win simply because the game rewards that cheap playstyle.
Some frustrated player might jump in and say, "skill issue," but it's not about that. I don’t care about ranking up—I care about fair, enjoyable matches. And right now, this game is anything but fair.

review:
I've played this since childhood. 75% of my gameplay has just been custom matches in kung foot, horde, team stock and brawlball, and nothing else much. When a battle pass comes out, I try to complete both tracks. This game is fun for a quick laugh with your mates but, if you are looking to play competitive, get ready to lose a lot of matches. This is normal in any game but it can be SUPER frustrating when you can't find players with a similar skillset, especially back in the days when there were plenty of players.

All I can say for playing ranked is to just make "Gold" rank your target. If you're willing to spend more than 500+ hours in this game, then good luck reaching plat and diamond. It was fun while it lasted but it is not worth the grind. Don't waste time like I have unless you just want to chill in custom lobbies.

review:
I've been playing this game for 120 hours in less than two months, and honestly, these have been the most frustrating two months of my life.
It feels like there are four types of players in this game:
The Normal One – Just plays the game normally. Unfortunately, almost no one does this.
The Jumper – Feels like his mom was bouncing on a trampoline while giving birth and decided to name him Spacebar.
Spam Sig – These people wake up and think, "How can I be as annoying as possible today?" Oh, right—by spamming signatures! They're usually not even good, they just win because they don’t let you touch them. I sincerely wish you all mental peace.
Passive Player – Just runs to the other side of the stage and waits for you to attack. They also jump a lot, and honestly, I have no clue how they enjoy the game.

That being said, the game is super fun, and nothing beats playing with your friends. I've already spent around $60 on skins, and I gotta say—it was worth it. The skins really make the experience feel different.
Do not play this game unless you know someone who's good at it, because progressing alone is insanely hard.
I’d give the game a 7/10, which is honestly pretty generous. It’s a simple game, but hey, it kills time.

review:
This game is fun and fiercely addictive. The gameplay is satisfying and feels good as long as you have a competent setup (high refresh monitor and a good keyboard), but become emotionally invested at your own peril.

I consider this game the absolute best mental resilience trainer ever created, bar none. No other experience looks as innocent as this while gently nudging you towards the borders of sanity. You will get frustrated at Brawlhalla.

As a way for someone to spend their free time, I would recommend you stick to playing with friends so at least you can all laugh about it. As for hitting ranked 1v1s, I would strongly recommend you do something you actually enjoy instead.

TL:DR - Enjoy in moderation ONLY

review:
The game is unbalanced AF. It currently has 15 weapons, which are:

Grapple Hammer: A good weapon if you play like a god and don’t miss a single hit. By the way, the damage is a bit lacking.

Sword: The noob weapon, basically it can stagger you with almost any directional hit, it’s very fast and has a broken up air aig.

Blasters: Were kind of trash a few patches ago, but now they do way too much damage for a weapon that hits so easily.

Rocket Lance: Another noob weapon, just spam any sigs and you can reach Platinum without even knowing how to play.

Spear: Average damage, good combos, was better in the past.

Katars: Very fast, fun to play, doesn’t do much damage, kind of broken ngl, but not as broken as some other weapons.

Axe: The third noob weapon, you can literally just spam light attacks and your opponent will be dead in no time.

Bow: Fast, good, and reliable weapon, but the damage is kind of lacking.

Gauntlets: Hard to master, but when you do, you’ll really get some hate messages.

Scythe: Damage is very lacking, like Gauntlets it’s hard to master, but when you do, you can basically 100 - 0 an opponent.

Cannon: Really underused, which is why it’s really broken. Too much damage, too much mobility, and like Scythe, it can 100 - 0 you in the hands of a good player.

Orb: Underused, which is why it has too much damage, but that being said, I don’t think it’s broken.

Greatsword: Hits really hard, feels broken, too much range, too much damage, super fast, it’s probably one of the most broken weapons in the game right now.

Battle Boots: Like Gauntlets, hard to master, but when you do, people will really hate you, It’s super fast and it can keep hitting without stopping;

Chakram: The newest weapon in Brawlhalla, was really broken, gives you a lot of movement control over your opponent. It was nerfed recently, but it’s still a really strong pick.

As you can see, we have a lot of options when it comes to weapons. The problem is, the ones that are strong are so much more broken compared to the others that it's infuriating. You can make a 20-hit combo on your opponent with a bow, but if he hits you 9 or 12 times with a Greatsword, you’re dead, let’s not even start with the sigs. And it's not like Greatsword is slow or anything it’s fast AF and has so much reach.

That being said, we haven’t even talked about the roster problem. Every new character comes with a more broken kit. It’s like every new character released, the power creep keeps going higher and higher compared to the older characters. If you want a broken character, look for the newly released ones.

That is what i have to say about the game, if you read until here thanks for the attention.

Disclaimer: Don’t come here defending the game like it's flawless, your comment will be ignored. Please do me and yourself a favor and keep my comment section clean.

author: {'steamid': '76561198985017122', 'num_games_owned': 52, 'num_reviews': 6, 'playtime_forever': 6003, 'playtime_last_two_weeks': 0, 'playtime_at_review': 5764, 'last_played': 1758511323}
review:
Let me preface this by saying I have played Brawlhalla. I have fought. I have suffered. I have stared into the void—and it stared back, dressed as a low-poly Viking with a sword too big for its animation budget. If you’re thinking of playing Brawlhalla, let me save you the trouble: just slam your head against a microwave for an hour while someone screams “GRAVITY CANCEL” in your ear. Same experience. Less trauma.

First off, the movement system is like trying to ice skate on a freshly polished greased-up Slip ‘N Slide while blindfolded. Why do all the characters feel like they’re made of helium and regret? You tap a direction and your character hurls themselves off the map like they’re trying to escape the game itself—and honestly, who can blame them?

Let’s talk about the hitboxes, which were clearly drawn by a sleep-deprived toddler using crayons and a Ouija board. I got smacked by an attack that happened behind the enemy. How? Why? Are we playing Brawlhalla or ghost tag?

And the weapons—oh my sweet agony. You pick up a weapon and suddenly your character transforms into a completely different person with a brand new moveset and absolutely zero sense of balance. Gauntlets? Congratulations, you're now an aerial war crime. Greatsword? Swing slower than evolution but hit like divine punishment. Blasters? Prepare to spam side light like it’s the only button on your controller—which, judging by the player base, it might be.

The community is a lawless wasteland powered by salt and anime rage. Ranked mode isn’t competitive—it’s psychological warfare. Every match is against a twelve-year-old with the reaction time of a caffeinated squirrel and the humility of a Roman emperor. Taunts after every kill. Spam after every win. It's like the game itself attracts people who peaked emotionally at age six.

And the aesthetics? It’s like someone tried to copy-paste a League of Legends splash art into a Saturday morning cartoon, but the file got corrupted halfway through. Every character is a bootleg version of a mythological figure or generic anime trope, and somehow all of them look like they’d sell you GFuel and betrayal.

Brawlhalla isn’t a game—it’s a social experiment gone terribly wrong. It’s a rage factory wrapped in a cartoon skin, powered by lag, imbalance, and pure chaos. If you’re looking for fun, go outside. If you’re looking for pain, welcome. You’ve found your new home.

Run. While you still can.

review:
Let me preface this by saying I have played Brawlhalla. I have fought. I have suffered. I have stared into the void—and it stared back, dressed as a low-poly Viking with a sword too big for its animation budget. If you’re thinking of playing Brawlhalla, let me save you the trouble: just slam your head against a microwave for an hour while someone screams “GRAVITY CANCEL” in your ear. Same experience. Less trauma.

First off, the movement system is like trying to ice skate on a freshly polished greased-up Slip ‘N Slide while blindfolded. Why do all the characters feel like they’re made of helium and regret? You tap a direction and your character hurls themselves off the map like they’re trying to escape the game itself—and honestly, who can blame them?

Let’s talk about the hitboxes, which were clearly drawn by a sleep-deprived toddler using crayons and a Ouija board. I got smacked by an attack that happened behind the enemy. How? Why? Are we playing Brawlhalla or ghost tag?

And the weapons—oh my sweet agony. You pick up a weapon and suddenly your character transforms into a completely different person with a brand new moveset and absolutely zero sense of balance. Gauntlets? Congratulations, you're now an aerial war crime. Greatsword? Swing slower than evolution but hit like divine punishment. Blasters? Prepare to spam side light like it’s the only button on your controller—which, judging by the player base, it might be.

The community is a lawless wasteland powered by salt and anime rage. Ranked mode isn’t competitive—it’s psychological warfare. Every match is against a twelve-year-old with the reaction time of a caffeinated squirrel and the humility of a Roman emperor. Taunts after every kill. Spam after every win. It's like the game itself attracts people who peaked emotionally at age six.

And the aesthetics? It’s like someone tried to copy-paste a League of Legends splash art into a Saturday morning cartoon, but the file got corrupted halfway through. Every character is a bootleg version of a mythological figure or generic anime trope, and somehow all of them look like they’d sell you GFuel and betrayal.

Brawlhalla isn’t a game—it’s a social experiment gone terribly wrong. It’s a rage factory wrapped in a cartoon skin, powered by lag, imbalance, and pure chaos. If you’re looking for fun, go outside. If you’re looking for pain, welcome. You’ve found your new home.

Run. While you still can.

review:
Allright let me preface this with, this game *was* great. Over the years, it has been absolutely ruined by metas. Axes, greatswords, and lances make this game incredibly frustrating, and much less enjoyable to play. A medium-experienced player could easily win against a veteran if they are simply on an axe with high damage. Every update they seem to add a new character that has broken weapons, and then nerf them just barely, making them much better than any older character.


I would recommend this as a party game, but honestly, winning public matches right now is less about whether you are better, and more about if you can spam metas or not. Until the game balances out a bit, I truly do not find it enjoyable.
I really wish it was less about metas, and more about who is better at lining up attacks, dodging, and hitting combos. And yeah yeah, "Skill issue" whatever.

review: After sitting in my account for over 4 years with only 4 hours of play time, I decided 3 days ago to actually give this game a chance. Here I am going into day 4, with 44 hours of play time. The legends are really fun. No aspect of this game can be considered pay-to-win. Though a bit pricey in my opinion, the skins for your legends are great, especially the crossovers. review:
There aren't enough insults that're allowed in reviews for me to sling at these idiots with how I feel right now.

tl;dr, cross-progress/platform/whatever system is complete garbage, and requires you to check in MONTHLY with every account linked to the game. Failure to do so un-links the account, and removes all of that crap from the other systems. I have, in the most dictionary-accurate usage of the word, LITERALLY NEVER SEEN THIS in another game or service.

Wouldn't you know it, trying to launch the game on PC now causes an instant crash, along with an error that's been a recurring problem for a few people since at LEAST 2014 with no fix. A+++ job guys, you'll get those dang bugs squashed someday, I'm sure! This is coupled with them going through Ubisoft for their console garbage, which... While this isn't Brawlhalla's fault specifically, it IS their fault they went with Ubisoft. The Switch can't load Ubisoft's sign-in page for Brawlhalla. Instead, you need to download a DIFFERENT Ubisoft game, and link your account with THAT game, and THEN Brawlhalla will be able to latch on too. Can't blame Ubisoft, it's probably the only way they can keep a single player signed in to whatever "Roller Champions" is.

I don't know what I expected, since they already handle their Twitch rewards campaign in the dumbest possible way too, using a stream extension to monitor viewtime/rewards, which just doesn't work for the majority of viewers. Or at all for me, because after numerous security exploits, I've disabled all Twitch extensions. Twitch drops wouldn't work much better, but then it's at least directly out of their hands.

tl;dr2: Fun game completely ruined by a bunch of hilariously stupid decisions both inside and outside of the game. If you're going to play, pick ONE system and never even *try* to engage in any of their extra garbage. If that system stops working then just quit playing. It isn't worth the frustration.

review:
TL;DR:
Brawlhalla was once a fun and competitive game, but its quality has declined significantly, especially in the past six months. The game now suffers from poor balance decisions, serious performance issues, and an overemphasis on monetizable content over gameplay improvements. Despite this, it can still be enjoyable in casual settings with friends.

Full Review:
First and foremost, I’ve played Brawlhalla far more than this account indicates. I started playing when the game was relatively new and have likely logged between 1,200 and 1,500 hours. With that context in mind, here’s my honest and detailed review:

Brawlhalla used to be a genuinely fun game. Depending on the game mode you play, it still might be, but overall, the game’s quality has declined drastically, especially over the last six months. It’s clear that the developers’ priorities have shifted significantly away from gameplay quality and competitive integrity.

Gameplay Issues and Balance Decisions:

One of the most glaring examples is the introduction, and subsequent neglect, of frustrating weapons like Battle Boots. Upon release, Battle Boots were extremely annoying to fight against. Many players disliked them, and they weren’t even fun to play as. Their strength came from easily executable, high-damage combos. Despite overwhelming community feedback, they went unchanged for several months.

Performance and Technical Problems:
This is arguably where the game has suffered the most, and the issues are constantly present. At this point, I can’t even launch the game without experiencing major performance problems within the first five minutes. These issues are widespread, ongoing, and affect nearly every match I play.

The anti-cheat system is a major contributor to the problem. Despite being highly invasive and resource-intensive, it does very little good for non-cheaters (due to how painfully easy it is to spot cheating). It also severely impacts the game's prediction system, which regularly fails during gameplay. Combine this with memory leaks and poor overall optimization, and the experience quickly becomes frustrating and inconsistent.
The effects are not subtle, they’re highly disruptive and frequent:
- Poor prediction leads to hit-sounds with no actual hits, characters teleporting mid-combat, players suddenly appearing inside or outside of attacks, and attacks executing instantly with no startup animation.
- Severe stuttering and lag spikes with a tencency to occur at the worst possible time, like just as you're being attacked, making it impossible to dodge.
- Overloaded servers result in wildly inconsistent latency. Brawlhalla is a game where timing is everything, and when server delay suddenly jumps from 20ms to 60–70ms, it completely throws off your timing and responsiveness, making it feel very sluggish, as if you are playing Queen Nai when you locked in Lin Fei.

This has gotten so bad that my friends and I now refer to it as a “Brawl-day”, basically, a term we use to describe whether the servers are usable that day or not. A bad Brawl-day means heavy delay, missed inputs, dropped dodges, and frustrating match after frustrating match.
These aren’t rare edge cases, they’re the norm for me and everyone I know who plays it. And the lack of action from the developers on these issues makes it feel like maintaining basic gameplay stability has taken a backseat to everything else.

Content Priorities Over Gameplay:
The focus has clearly shifted toward monetizable content, such as frequent crossover characters and new maps. Unfortunately, these additions often worsen the gameplay experience:
- Many crossovers are visually and audibly confusing, making it difficult to read their attacks.
- New maps frequently introduce chaotic and unnecessary mechanics (e.g., platforms that move on two axis, lava hazards, parts of the stage moving) that hurt visibility and gameplay clarity. The most recent map is so visually unclear that my duo partner and I have banned it from our matches.
- It’s evident that most development resources are going toward marketable content instead of balancing characters or fixing critical performance issues.

Community Experience:
- While not necessarily the developers’ fault, the game’s community has become increasingly toxic. Expect to encounter players who spam signatures, weapon-starve in casual modes and use emotes to taunt. This trend mirrors toxicity found in many online games today.

Despite its flaws, Brawlhalla can still be fun in casual settings. I continue to play it occasionally, just not competitively. Custom games or 2v2 matches with friends, especially with random character selection, can still provide a great time. Playing without the stress of ranked competition helps avoid the more frustrating aspects of the game.

Brawlhalla wasn’t always like this. When the developers focused on gameplay and competitive integrity, it was one of the most enjoyable games out there. Every time I launch it, I hope the team rediscovers that vision and restores the game to its former glory.

Brawlhalla is a fun, fast-paced platform fighter that’s easy to jump into but offers a ton of depth for those who want to master it. The controls are smooth and responsive, and each Legend brings their own unique flair with different weapons and playstyles. Whether you're playing casually with friends or diving into ranked matches, there's always a good time to be had.

One of the best things about Brawlhalla is its accessibility. It's free to play, supports cross-platform multiplayer, and doesn’t overwhelm new players with complicated mechanics. The game is constantly updated with new content, events, and characters — including fun crossovers that bring in popular franchises for a fresh twist.

It’s a great choice for fans of competitive brawlers or anyone looking for a fun, skill-based game with a lighthearted vibe. Brawlhalla may look simple on the surface, but it’s packed with satisfying gameplay, strong community support, and endless replayability.

review: Brawlhalla is a very exciting and dynamic fighting game that I have enjoyed playing since 2018. author: {'steamid': '76561198159985709', 'num_games_owned': 0, 'num_reviews': 23, 'playtime_forever': 3954, 'playtime_last_two_weeks': 0, 'playtime_at_review': 3954, 'last_played': 1638868708}
review:
So there I was, cruising in glorious Diamond rank on my main, firing off combos like a digital Picasso, when bam! the devs dropped a handful of updates. At first, I shrugged—“Cool, new balance tweaks, more shinies,” right? Nope. Suddenly my bullets mistimed like a sleepwalking drummer, my ultimates vanished into the void, and my sword swings… well, they vanished too. It felt like the game was playing favorites, giving my enemies’ attacks a VIP pass through my defenses while mine got stuck in traffic.

Was it magic? Dark sorcery? Or just a sneaky ping gremlin messing with my packets? I tried everything: rebooting, changing servers, even offering sacrifices to the old lag gods. Nada. While my foes gleefully danced through my “shield” grins, I stood there looking like a clown at a mime convention, waving melee strikes into the ether.

Look, I’m no noob—I cracked the meta quicker than a peanut, hit Diamond before lunch, and had more MVP ribbons than a trophy cabinet. But these patches… man, they felt like the game itself looked me dead in the pixels and said, “Nah, we don’t want you.” So I did the unthinkable—I hung up my headset, marched out of queue, and cried digital tears into the void of “How could they do me dirty like this?”

And that, my friends, is why you might find my account gathering dust. Because when your own game stops acknowledging your awesomeness, you know it’s time to ride off into the sunset… or at least until the next hotfix. 🚀🎮😭

You know that feeling when you stub your toe, step on a Lego, and get dumped all in the same minute? That’s Brawlhalla. This game is an unbalanced, rage-inducing dumpster fire run by people who clearly gave up after the first patch.

Sigs. Fucking. Everywhere.
Pick any legend. Doesn’t matter. Spam the same brain-dead signature move 900 times and BOOM — you're a "pro." There is zero punishment for button mashing, zero effort in movement, and zero fucking balance. Sword? Cheese. Spear? Cheese. Greatsword? Rotting, moldy cheese left out in the sun. If you like actual combos or thoughtful gameplay, get the hell out now. This is a glorified sig simulator.

Matchmaking is rigged by Satan himself.
One match you're fighting toddlers with broken controllers, the next you're up against a crackhead esports demon who reads your soul and dodges mid-air like he's playing in The Matrix. Ranked? Don't even bother unless you enjoy being gaslit by the Elo system and developing anger issues.

Hitboxes? What hitboxes?
I got hit by a move in a different zip code. Meanwhile, I land a perfectly timed side-light into recovery and the game just shrugs like, “Nah, bro.”

And the community?
Imagine being tea-bagged by a 12-year-old who just won by mashing down-sig on Petra for 4 minutes. Now imagine that every. single. game. Welcome to Brawlhalla.

TL;DR:
This game is a cracked-out clown fiesta with the balance of a one-legged table and the community of a warzone. I hate it. I can’t stop playing. Please send help.

0/10
I’d rather eat glass than queue ranked again.

review:
The amount of time I've spent in this game would be surprising considering the score I'm giving it, but I cannot seriously recommend Brawlhalla when there are so many better ways to use your time. There's NO community in any online game I've faced (not even other F2P games such as LoL) that is as toxic as this one is. If you don't live close to one of the servers for this game your connection is jsut utter garbage. You're always gona have some sort of input lag. If you've ever played any fighting game you'll realize this game is very unbalanced and devs just cycle through metas to hype the tournaments up basically as they know exactly what they're doing and it's not balance. There's no penalty for doing or not doing stuff here (NO Rock Paper Scissors type of design you find in literally EVERY OTHER FIGHTING GAME). The whole economy behind this game revolves around being an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, taunts are the best selling in-app purchase by a mile. If you don't live in the US (or one of the 1st world countries) then good luck trying to buy anything as the premium in-game currency price isn't region adjusted. The more you play and the farther you get (up to Diamond) the more passive and boring the game becomes. There's footsies, there's defensive oriented characters in other fighting games but this is ridiculous... some matches will be stalemates where your opponent will literally just run away. As a matter of a fact, running away is objectively more effective than anythign else which is an incentive to play passively. Why? Because you have more options to run away, dodge, defend, throw your weapon, etc than you have to approach. Why would I recommend a game whose population is mostly kids yet it has the most toxic players ever? Everyone is tired ofthe toxicity, of the passiveness and the overall same-ness of the game. You don't have to believe me if you don't want to, few people really talk about this but it is the truth. You can check "toxicity Brawlhalla" on Youtube...

YouTube™ Video: My Opinion On The State Of Brawlhalla After A One Year Hiatus

This video does NOT mean that I am quitting Brawlhalla. Its only purpose is to give a detailed explanation of why I dislike playing this game in high ELO and why I intend to remain a casual player.


https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZgVflTtAXM

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_jUMcof1Llk

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8fSapMtS0LU

The game promotes a competitive scene, yet it lacks any balance to it. The fact they don't do anything about it yet they pour a new skin or toxic taunt every other month tells you what the developers' priorities are (its a business after all). Toxicity is a moneymaker. Even Brawlhalla's top players complain about the things mentioned and even more, yet in years those complaints have not been adressed at all. Boomie (#1-2 player depending on the year) has complained about a lot of stuff throughout the years, Sandstorm (undeniably #1) focuses on playing Smash competitively yet he absolutely DESTROYS this scene, eggsoup (ex-top 8 regular) constantly points out the problems with the community and the meta, dopameme (one of the guys who made the best exhibition combo videos) has complained and left the competitive scene due to several instances of lacking balance. These are people that have thousands of hours poured in the game and they all agree with this.

Most Brawlhalla players will defend the game till the end as a fighting game but have never ever played other fighting games in their life. Being toxic and sending death threats and generally inappropiate slurs is the name of the meta.

The game is addicting, not gonna lie, but I do not recommend it when you have to face an absurd amount of toxicity if you're a casual and an insanely passive and unbalanced meta if you're playing competitively.

review: It's a platform fighter, but pretty alright. The system of weapons that are the same across characters with slight variations isn't my style but I can appreciate high skill expression with low entry barriers. author: {'steamid': '76561198071604159', 'num_games_owned': 356, 'num_reviews': 111, 'playtime_forever': 20, 'playtime_last_two_weeks': 0, 'playtime_at_review': 20, 'last_played': 1746739475}
review:
Brawlhalla is often praised as a free-to-play alternative to Super Smash Bros., but after spending countless hours with the game, I can confidently say that it’s a shallow, frustrating, and ultimately unsatisfying experience. While it may have a dedicated fanbase, the game is riddled with issues that make it more of a chore to play than a genuinely fun fighting game. Here’s why Brawlhalla fails to live up to the hype.

1. Repetitive, Floaty Gameplay
One of the biggest problems with Brawlhalla is its core gameplay mechanics. The movement feels weightless and imprecise, making every character control like they’re floating on ice. Unlike Smash Bros., where characters have distinct weight and momentum, Brawlhalla’s fighters all feel like reskins of the same few archetypes. This lack of depth makes matches feel repetitive, as there’s little variation in how different characters play.

The combat itself is overly simplistic, relying too much on spamming the same few moves. Since most attacks have minimal startup or endlag, matches often devolve into mindless button-mashing rather than strategic play. The game’s emphasis on aerial combat also means that ground play is nearly irrelevant, further limiting the skill ceiling.

2. Uninspired Character Design
While Brawlhalla boasts a large roster, most characters are forgettable and lack personality. Unlike Smash Bros., where each fighter has a unique moveset and identity, Brawlhalla’s legends feel like they were designed by a committee trying to check off a list of weapon types rather than create compelling characters.

Even worse, many characters share the same weapons, meaning their movesets overlap significantly. This leads to a sense of déjà vu when playing different fighters, as you’ll often see the same animations and combos repeated across the roster. The game tries to compensate with crossover skins (like WWE or Adventure Time characters), but these feel like cheap cash grabs rather than meaningful additions.

3. Pay-to-Win (Sort Of) and Grindy Progression
While Brawlhalla is technically free-to-play, it employs some of the most aggressive monetization tactics in the genre. The game locks nearly every cosmetic behind a paywall or an absurdly long grind, making it feel like a glorified demo unless you’re willing to spend money.

Even worse, the way characters are rotated in the free roster means you’re often forced to either grind for weeks to unlock a single fighter or pay up. This creates an artificial barrier to enjoying the game, especially when certain characters are objectively stronger than others. While it’s not strictly "pay-to-win," the system is designed to pressure players into spending money just to have access to a full experience.

4. Terrible Online Experience
Brawlhalla’s netcode is notoriously inconsistent. Even with a strong internet connection, matches often suffer from lag, input delay, and teleporting players. The ranked mode is especially frustrating, as a single lag spike can ruin an otherwise competitive match.

Additionally, the matchmaking system is unbalanced. New players frequently get matched against veterans with hundreds of hours of experience, leading to one-sided stomps that aren’t fun for anyone. The lack of proper regional servers also means that cross-continent matches are common, exacerbating the lag issues.

5. Lack of Meaningful Single-Player Content
If you’re not into online multiplayer, Brawlhalla offers almost nothing of value. The "training" mode is barebones, the "story" is nonexistent, and the AI opponents range from brain-dead to unfairly punishing with no middle ground. Even the "Brawl of the Week" events are just recycled game modes with minor tweaks.

Compared to Smash Bros., which offers a rich single-player experience with Classic Mode, Adventure Mode, and Spirit Battles, Brawlhalla feels barren. It’s clear that the developers put minimal effort into offline content, making the game feel like a hollow shell unless you’re willing to suffer through its online modes.

6. Toxic Community
While this isn’t entirely the game’s fault, Brawlhalla has one of the most toxic player bases in the fighting game community. Taunting, trolling, and BMing are rampant, and the game’s barebones reporting system does little to curb bad behavior. The ranked mode is especially bad, with players frequently disconnecting or spamming the same moves to exploit the game’s poor balance.

Conclusion: A Mediocre Smash Clone with No Soul
Brawlhalla isn’t the worst game ever made, but it’s a prime example of wasted potential. Instead of refining its mechanics or adding depth, the developers have focused on pumping out uninspired crossover skins and milking players for microtransactions. The gameplay is repetitive, the characters are forgettable, and the online experience is plagued with issues.

If you’re looking for a deep, rewarding platform fighter, stick with Super Smash Bros. or Rivals of Aether. Brawlhalla is a shallow, frustrating experience that doesn’t deserve the attention it gets. Save your time and play something better.

Final Rating: 3/10 – A forgettable, frustrating mess with little redeeming value.

review:
Please ignore the mouth breathers with 2k hours leaving negative reviews, their brains can't comprehend the idea that them spending thousands of hours on a game might mean they actually like it despite its flaws.

Its a free game that provides very solid competitive platform fighting gameplay, and is especially good with friends due to how easy it is to play together. The game balance and monetization (they just released a 35 dollar skin) can be frustrating/poor at times but, again, it is a free video game. You lose nothing trying it out. 

With that being said, this is one of those games with a very high skill ceiling and a community that has spent thousands of hours perfecting the mechanics, so being a new player can be rough. Despite what some people may say, pretty much every match is decided by who is the better player. There isn't much you can do about other than just buckling up and learning the game or bringing a friend along to make practicing more fun. 

The community can also be quite toxic at times, but that is the nature of basically any competitive video game, you'll be able to get over it. 

Lastly there is rollback netcode, which can make things feel a bit clunky or laggy at times (sometimes your game will make a sound that you hit someone but they won't actually get hit), but is ultimately more positive than negative as it makes the game less ping dependent.

review: This is the most god awful game I have ever played. This game is so unbalanced you would have better balance surfing a turtle mid air and landing and surviving. Speaking of turtles. Who decided on Imugi bro. I've been a religious player of Brawlhalla and if playing Brawlhalla proved anything, it proved there is no God. Why on earth is there not Sig Fatigue? The entire game would be balanced if there was Sig Fatigue. On that topic of fatigue, why on earth is the maps either too small or too big. When I play ranked and I launch a Cassidy to Mars, she shouldn't comeback down being able to swing her hammer and send me to Egypt and I die. Also what are the buffs in this game?? Why does Cassidy, a cowgirl, have more defense then jhala, a literal trained warrior. What sense does that make!? I play this game to relax. If I'm being honest, I mean truly honest, I thank you Brawlhalla Team. I thank you, because whenever I play this game, I'm reminded that I don't have to play. This game builds up so much hate in me that I remember outside is free too and so is Fortnite. I love this game with the bottom of my heart. But once Smash Bros gets ported to Steam and it will, I won't ever look back. Until then, keep making unbalanced characters and keep giving them unbalnced items like Boots. Did I mention how much I hate boots? Why are there true combos and guaranteed attacks in a fighting game. Let that sink in. In a shooting game, should there also be guaranteed 4 bullets that hit your character before you have to take control of the aim? If you answered yes, stop developing games. I am willing to work with the developers as an intern to fix the wrongs. I really want to see this game thrive. But the only time this game thrives, is when it's turned off. The only time I'm reminded of this game, is when I have so much success in my life I just want to make myself mad. So I turn on Brawlhalla. My friends ask me how I'm so good at Smash Bros I tell them my next option was Brawlhalla. When I see my mom and she asks me how my day is I tell her "I fought a Loki" and she makes me dinner because she knows my day was ruined. I made Youtube Videos on Brawlhalla and had fun. I will make some soon. But I feel like I'm drinking. Feeding a poison to my body for enjoyment. All this can be fixed if you just add sig fatigue. I know you can. Or maybe even a shielding gimmick like your older better brother that I won't know and is most definitely not Super Smash Bros For the Nintendo. Listen, you reader who reads this. If you happen to find yourself playing Brawlhalla just know, you are playing a battle against yourself. I am being as nice as possible. I've been playing for 7 years. I took a 3 year break. So I've been playing for 4 years. I come back and suddenly I have Tai Lung stringing me across the world and a turtle who can tank sigs like they're light attacks. I already have 122 hours on this game on steam. This is sad. I will edit this later. After losing my ranked games (which I won 1 and went up 13 and loss 1 and went down 17 make that make sense) I am tired. Reading this, I feel tired. But sending this in hopes it reaches 1 developer makes me happy. I hope this game stays around for another 20 years. I want to make my children play this game for punishment. Whenever I am asked to host a game night, I won't play Mario Kart that's way better. I'll turn on Brawlhalla that's free and everyone will hate me. Brawlhalla is the equivalent of talking about politics at the Thanksgiving Table. The worst part is, the game's not even bad. It's just so unbalanced I can't believe the developers actually test this and say "yeah this is good to release." Please, hire me as an intern. I will fix this. I have experience in C++, Java, Unreal, Unity. If I need more experience I will do anything to add sig fatigue.

review: its so ass dont play it, it often faces criticism regarding its balance, as some Legends and weapon combinations are perceived as significantly stronger, leading to uneven matches. Many players also find the gameplay can become repetitive, despite the variety of characters and weapons, especially when encountering similar tactics or opponents repeatedly. Another point of contention is the prevalence of "spamming," where players rely on repeatedly using the same attacks, which can feel frustrating and lacking in strategic depth. For newcomers, the learning curve can be quite steep, as a comprehensive tutorial for all the techniques and characters might be missing. Furthermore, some players experience issues with lag and unstable connections, which can severely impact the gameplay, particularly in ranked matches. There's also a perception that the developers sometimes prioritize new cosmetic items over addressing balance problems or bugs within the game. The matchmaking system is another area of criticism, as it can occasionally pair players with vastly different skill levels, resulting in unbalanced and unenjoyable matches. The training mode, while present, is considered by some to be insufficient for effectively learning the game's more advanced mechanics and strategies. Depending on the time of day and game mode, queue times for finding a match can also be lengthy. Lastly, as with many online games, Brawlhalla has its share of players who exhibit unsportsmanlike behavior or engage in toxic communication, which can negatively affect the overall atmosphere.

review:
Was curious to see how this outlasted so many other platform fighters. It's because it's so accessible. Simple attacks allow players to focus more on dashing, air juggling and edge guarding. Characters each have two unique combinations of weapons with their own flair on special attacks and some minor stat differences. Currently a 61 character roster but it's not as though you have to learn 61 matchups and you can just play whoever looks the coolest.

Free to play and cross-play make finding a game near instantaneous. Ranked 1v1 and 2v2. Taunts and post fight emojis (albeit toxic). Rage quitters turn into bots. All characters are unlockable through an easily obtainable currency. Cosmetics cost a premium but nobody is making you buy them.

review:
🛡️ Brawlhalla - Fun, Fast, and Free
Brawlhalla is one of those games that’s easy to pick up, but hard to master. It looks simple at first, but there’s a lot of depth once you get into it.

What I Like:

Tons of unique characters (called Legends), each with different weapons and styles.

The combat is smooth, fast-paced, and really fun.

You can play online, offline, ranked, or just casually with friends.

Cross-platform works great — I play with friends on console while I'm on PC.

It’s completely free and not pay-to-win.

What I Don’t Like:

Some matchmaking can feel unfair, especially at low ranks.

The community can be toxic sometimes, like in most competitive games.

Cosmetics are a bit expensive if you care about looks.

Still, I keep coming back because it’s just that fun. Whether you're messing around in free-for-alls or going all-in on ranked 1v1s, Brawlhalla delivers.

Final : 8.5/10 — Worth playing, especially with friends.

review: Don't get me wrong i used to like this game but i need to criticize this game for its current state because there can't be a chance for this game to get better if someone like me doesn't. I used to play this i would say 2020 as a free game since i was a young teen with no money. Game was somewhat simple and had barely a skill ceiling to get decent at the game which was good enough for me to get better, now i see that it is NOT friendly for new players. I have played a bit recently and holy hell causal feels like a ranked match. I would get the sweatiest players as if like they lived in the game. Now with the amount of hours i put in u would except me to be able to counter them and yes i do beat these people most of the time but this is CASUAL. This tells me the player base is dying a bit or lack of a matchmaking system which is also a issue the game has had for a while. Now my guess to see why the casual players are not here no more is pretty obvious with the part i just mentioned, another would be how absolutely broken the new characters they add are and the no re balancing of the game. For example when priya first came out before there were any real priya sweats, people would spam the hell out of her signatures with little to no light attacks with hardly room to dodge and she would win. This game BADLY NEEDS re-balancing in the characters and the mechanics but i do not see it happening anytime soon since they prioritize making money not to mention they heavily prioritize the meta characters and newer characters leaving other characters in the dust. In the dust as well is the casual players like me who just want to have fun and have a good fun match without having it act like the game was for the death and to pass on the bloodline.

review:
Brawlhalla is a free-to-play platform fighter that blends chaotic brawling with a diverse roster of characters. With about 68 hours played, I wouldn’t call myself a high-level player—but I’ve had plenty of fun, especially with friends. That said, it’s definitely a game that shines in the right context.

🟢 Pros:
Super Fun with Friends
This is where Brawlhalla really comes to life. Whether it’s 1v1s, team fights, or chaotic 4-player free-for-alls, it’s easy to jump in and start having a blast. It’s the kind of game that’s best enjoyed with some friendly trash talk and laughter.

Easy to Learn, Hard to Master
The controls are accessible, and you can start pulling off cool moves pretty quickly. But once you start climbing the skill curve, you’ll realize there’s a surprising amount of depth—timing, spacing, matchups, and movement all matter a lot.

Big Roster of Unique Characters
With tons of Legends and crossover characters, there’s something for everyone. Each weapon combo feels different, which keeps things fresh.

Free-to-Play Without Being Pay-to-Win
You can unlock everything through gameplay, and purchases are mostly cosmetic. That’s a big plus.

🔴 Cons:
Not as Fun Solo
While it’s a solid game overall, playing solo just doesn’t have the same appeal. Without friends, the fun and chaos feel a bit hollow, and ranked mode can feel frustrating or overly sweaty if you're not trying to "git gud."

Learning Curve Can Get Steep
Once you hit a certain skill level (or face players who live in ranked), the gap becomes noticeable. It’s not a huge issue, but casual players might feel outpaced.

Repetitive if You're Not Progressing
If you're not working toward a rank or grinding for unlocks, the matches can start to feel samey after a while—especially solo.

Final Thoughts:
Brawlhalla is a blast when played with friends. It’s approachable, fun, and has enough depth to keep you coming back—if you have the right group to enjoy it with. On your own, it’s a bit less compelling, but still a solid, well-made fighter that deserves its spot in the genre.

Rating: 7.5/10 – A party brawler at heart. Great with friends, less so solo—but always solid.

review: This is the most god awful game I have ever played. This game is so unbalanced you would have better balance surfing a turtle mid air and landing and surviving. Speaking of turtles. Who decided on Imugi bro. I've been a religious player of Brawlhalla and if playing Brawlhalla proved anything, it proved there is no God. Why on earth is there not Sig Fatigue? The entire game would be balanced if there was Sig Fatigue. On that topic of fatigue, why on earth is the maps either too small or too big. When I play ranked and I launch a Cassidy to Mars, she shouldn't comeback down being able to swing her hammer and send me to Egypt and I die. Also what are the buffs in this game?? Why does Cassidy, a cowgirl, have more defense then jhala, a literal trained warrior. What sense does that make!? I play this game to relax. If I'm being honest, I mean truly honest, I thank you Brawlhalla Team. I thank you, because whenever I play this game, I'm reminded that I don't have to play. This game builds up so much hate in me that I remember outside is free too and so is Fortnite. I love this game with the bottom of my heart. But once Smash Bros gets ported to Steam and it will, I won't ever look back. Until then, keep making unbalanced characters and keep giving them unbalnced items like Boots. Did I mention how much I hate boots? Why are there true combos and guaranteed attacks in a fighting game. Let that sink in. In a shooting game, should there also be guaranteed 4 bullets that hit your character before you have to take control of the aim? If you answered yes, stop developing games. I am willing to work with the developers as an intern to fix the wrongs. I really want to see this game thrive. But the only time this game thrives, is when it's turned off. The only time I'm reminded of this game, is when I have so much success in my life I just want to make myself mad. So I turn on Brawlhalla. My friends ask me how I'm so good at Smash Bros I tell them my next option was Brawlhalla. When I see my mom and she asks me how my day is I tell her "I fought a Loki" and she makes me dinner because she knows my day was ruined. I made Youtube Videos on Brawlhalla and had fun. I will make some soon. But I feel like I'm drinking. Feeding a poison to my body for enjoyment. All this can be fixed if you just add sig fatigue. I know you can. Or maybe even a shielding gimmick like your older better brother that I won't know and is most definitely not Super Smash Bros For the Nintendo. Listen, you reader who reads this. If you happen to find yourself playing Brawlhalla just know, you are playing a battle against yourself. I am being as nice as possible. I've been playing for 7 years. I took a 3 year break. So I've been playing for 4 years. I come back and suddenly I have Tai Lung stringing me across the world and a turtle who can tank sigs like they're light attacks. I already have 122 hours on this game on steam. This is sad. I will edit this later. After losing my ranked games (which I won 1 and went up 13 and loss 1 and went down 17 make that make sense) I am tired. Reading this, I feel tired. But sending this in hopes it reaches 1 developer makes me happy. I hope this game stays around for another 20 years. I want to make my children play this game for punishment. Whenever I am asked to host a game night, I won't play Mario Kart that's way better. I'll turn on Brawlhalla that's free and everyone will hate me. Brawlhalla is the equivalent of talking about politics at the Thanksgiving Table. The worst part is, the game's not even bad. It's just so unbalanced I can't believe the developers actually test this and say "yeah this is good to release." Please, hire me as an intern. I will fix this. I have experience in C++, Java, Unreal, Unity. If I need more experience I will do anything to add sig fatigue.

review:
I've played Brawlhalla for around 4 hours and really enjoyed it. The controls are tight and responsive, and the combat feels smooth and fast-paced. It’s easy to get into, but there’s clearly a lot of depth to master.

However, I did notice some lag during online matches — which was surprising since I have a stable 100 Mbps connection. After checking, I realized the issue isn’t with speed, but likely due to server lag or high ping. It could also be the server region or Wi-Fi instability, even though everything else works fine online.

If the netcode or regional matchmaking gets a bit more optimized, this would be a solid 5-star game. Still, it’s an awesome free-to-play experience and definitely worth trying if you enjoy fighting games.

review:
Honestly, Brawlhalla is just a super fun game. I started playing it not expecting much, but I quickly got hooked. It’s easy to pick up, even if you’re not great at fighting games. The controls are simple, but the gameplay still has depth, so you can actually get better and learn cool strategies over time.

One thing I really like is how many characters (Legends) there are — each one feels different, so you’re not stuck doing the same thing over and over. Plus, the game is totally free, and you can even play with friends on different consoles, which is awesome.

I’d recommend Brawlhalla to anyone who likes fast-paced games or wants something competitive without being too serious. Whether you’re playing casually or trying to climb the ranked ladder, it’s just a great time. And the devs are always adding new stuff, so it never really gets boring.

review:
[h1] The Game Stays the Same... [/h1]

New collaborations.
More characters.
More stages.
And the same frantic, lighthearted, fun spirit.
Here, the only thing you need is just the will to have fun, to try, to laugh when you get blasted off the map,
or when you land that miraculous hit at the last second.


[h2] The Tryhard Hell [/h2]


But let’s be real.
Brawlhalla has a dark side.
No, not the lore.
The tryhards.

Players who treat this like Olympic qualifiers.
People who don’t play: they execute.
People who don’t laugh: they calculate.

And then it becomes another game.
A more tense, more brutal one.
One where, if you’re still laughing,
it’s probably because you haven’t seen the infinite aerial combo that’s about to make you reflect on your life choices.


[h2] Conclusion [/h2]


Brawlhalla is a game to play with friends.
To laugh your ass off.
To trash-talk lovingly and go another round.
Not to suffer in ranked.

review:
My friend got me into this game 2 years ago and we used to have a lot of fun playing it, but then they started changing the mechanics more and more, basically making you re-learn the game every time. On top of that it often doesn't count your attack even when it comes out before your opponent's attack, making the game really frustrating. It's clear that the devs are money hungry thus putting out new legends and skins all the time, buffing the newer legends with each update. Also the ranked queue feels like it's broken as the game either queues you with diamonds or silvers, no matter your current rank. Sometimes the servers feel like they're way too laggy, other times you'll only match with greatsword or boots legends, spamming all over the stage, which greatsword and boots legends have a large attack radius with their heavy attacks, making it harder to land. If they end up winning they think that they're the next Sandstorm or Boomie, if they lose they cry by spamming the down-thumbs, adding you on steam trying to tell you to kys irl, inviting you to a room or spamming the rematch button. 

The devs act like they care about the fanbase by putting out surveys and "banning" toxic behaviour from the game. They literally removed the game chat and will ban you from tournaments when voicing your opinion through any other platform, yet you can buy many toxic taunts and emojis, such as the saltcan, the throne, the laughing, the W-stance etc. 

This hides the toxicity of the game outwardly, but inside the game this mentality is still very present and they support it.

On top of that, the toxicity is crazy. People will do the most brainless sh*t all game, still win because the hitreg is a coin flip if you don't live near the servers (I live in Hungary and have to use German servers) then spam random emotes on the end screen, being hella proud of themselves I'm sure. review:
Lo, hearken unto mine words, for I have taken upon mine own self the grievous task of playing Brawlhalla, a game so foul and vexing that it doth bring neither mirth nor joy, but only wroth and lamentation.

From the first moment mine eyes did alight upon its gaudy visage, I perceived its lack of substance. The characters, aye, many in number, yet all art shallow as a dried-up well. Though they boast many a skin and garish costume, they possess no soul nor depth. 'Tis as if one were to dine upon a feast of painted wax—fair to the eye, yet barren to the taste.

The controls—ye gods!—they be as if devised by a drunken knave with nary a thought to grace or flow. The combat, which ought to be noble and artful, is naught but a flurry of hapless flailings. Each match descendeth into chaos, where skill be cast aside like a crumpled parchment and chance doth rule as king.

The community, too, is most foul. A den of knavish curs and braggarts, who knoweth not the meaning of honour nor civility. Rarely hath I encountered such a rabble of ill-mannered youths, shrieking into the void with tongues of venom and pride.

And what, I pray, is the purpose of this grind eternal? To unlock ever more trinkets and trifles? To climb a ladder of smoke and shadow, only to be cast down by fools and lag alike? I say nay! I would sooner wrestle with a mad boar than endure another hour of such tedious strife.

Verily, Brawlhalla is but a hollow echo of worthier games, a jest most cruel upon those who seek valorous battle. Let it be cast into the pit, and its name spoken no more.

I endeth this revieuw with but one counsel: Flee, good folk, and play it not.

—A sorely displeasèd player, most weary and wroth
