review:
I wanted to like Brawlhalla. It looks like a fun, free alternative to Smash Bros., but the reality is a shallow, unbalanced brawler with one of the worst communities I’ve ever experienced in an online game.

Tezca: The Poster Child of Bad Design
Let’s talk about Tezca — possibly the most annoying, broken legend in the entire roster. His moveset is basically a spammer’s dream. Wild hitboxes, ridiculous priority, and way too much mobility for how hard he hits. It feels like the devs just threw balance out the window and gave him everything. And of course, every Tezca main plays exactly the same: dodge in, mash sigs, taunt, repeat. It’s less like fighting a player and more like battling a YouTube tutorial on how to ruin ranked queues.

Toxic Playerbase:
The community doesn’t help. Win or lose, expect emote spam, taunts, and messages like “ez” after every match — especially from Tezca players. New players get stomped and mocked constantly, and there’s little to no in-game support to deal with harassment or trolling. It’s a breeding ground for ego and bad manners.

Boring and Repetitive Combat:
Once you’ve played a few hours, you’ve basically seen everything. Matches blur together because most players just abuse the same strong characters (Tezca, Mordex, etc.) and spam the same moves. There's very little variety or creativity in playstyle anymore.

Lag, Grind, and Greed:
Add in inconsistent servers, a ridiculous grind for unlocking legends, and overpriced cosmetic bundles (especially the crossovers), and you’ve got a game that feels more like a cash grab than a passion project.

Verdict:
If you’re into clunky combat, sweaty spammers, and the occasional rage-inducing Tezca mirror match, Brawlhalla might be for you. For everyone else — especially if you value balance and a decent community — do yourself a favor and skip it.

review:
Brawlhalla: My Favourite Psychological Torture Simulator

Shit game.
Shit developers.
Down a controller.
Down a part of my soul.
Down horrendously in ranked and in life.

Let me make this painfully clear: I hate this game. I hate it on a level that transcends logic. Like Brawlhalla was coded specifically to ruin my day. Like I accidentally stepped on the lead developer’s cat and they cursed my account forever. Every time I load in, I feel like I’m signing a contract with the devil, written in broken hit boxes and dodges that defy physics.

BMG—Blue Mammoth Games—I don’t know what kind of Ouija-board-led update strategy you’re following, but whatever dark ritual you’re using to balance this game has worked. I now experience anger on a cellular level. You’ve created a platform fighter that fights me back. Not just my character—me, as a person. 

I feel nothing but pure, venomous, undiluted hatred towards you for the rage I’ve been forced to endure. You’ve caused me to develop emotional trauma from sigs. My thumbs twitch when I hear the ranked queue sound. And yet—I keep playing. Like a clown. A sweaty, broken, rocket-lance-gaped clown.

I would recommend Brawlhalla if:
You want to develop anger issues that follow you offline.


You’re curious about what Caner™ is. (It’s not cancer. It’s worse. It’s a slow mental decay caused by Lance mains)


You love getting anally violated by a projectile the size of a Fiat 500 flying at Mach 4 from across the stage.


You enjoy hovering in high plat, fully convinced you’re better than this, only to get three-stocked by someone mashing light attacks while emoting mid-combo.


You want to experience a full emotional breakdown in 6 minutes, with cartoon graphics and lo-fi menu music as the soundtrack.


This game has ruined friendships, broken controllers, and taken me to places emotionally I don’t think therapy can reach. It’s not just a game—it’s a toxic relationship with better combos.
The worst part? I’ll reinstall the game tomorrow.
Grinding.
Coping.
Telling myself that this is the game I climb to diamond in.

Final score:

Visuals: Innocently deceptive.


Gameplay: A war crime/masochism


Soundtrack: Banger.


Mental stability: None


Controller life expectancy: 3 matches max.


Would I recommend it?

Only if you hate yourself enough.
Only if you’re ready to meet your inner demons mid-match.
Only if you’re built for pain.
Only if your feeling mentally stable and you want to fix that.

review:
Brawlhalla: A Beautiful, Button-Mashing Nightmare That I Can’t Stop Playing

Let’s get one thing straight: Brawlhalla is the kind of game that will make you question your skills, your sanity, and your friendships—but somehow, you’ll keep coming back for more. It’s like an abusive relationship where the punches are literal and the betrayal comes in the form of being combo’d off the stage by a spamming Orion for the seventh time in a row.

At its core, Brawlhalla is a free-to-play platform fighter where up to four players beat the ever-living pixels out of each other with swords, guns, gauntlets, and whatever else the 50+ characters decide to bring to the party. Each match starts out fun and chaotic—and ends with you getting three-stocked by a 12-year-old who only uses side light, side sig, repeat.

Want to play casually? Too bad. Every quickplay match is a sweat-fest, where every opponent is either a keyboard warrior with 3,000 hours or a mobile player who still somehow dodges better than you. Ranked? That’s where dreams go to die. One moment you're in Gold, the next you’re in Elo purgatory wondering how that unarmed combo sent you to the shadow realm.

And the characters? Oh, they’re fun… until you realize some of them were clearly born in the fires of imbalance. You’ll find your main, you’ll love them—then you'll run into a Hattori who makes you uninstall the game mid-match. There’s variety, sure, but it’s hard to enjoy when every match turns into “which legend can spam their sigs faster and get away with it.”

But here’s the worst part: it is fun. The movement is clean, the mechanics deceptively deep, and those moments when you actually pull off a combo or edgeguard? Pure serotonin. You’ll scream in victory one second and rage-quit the next. It’s the gaming equivalent of eating spicy food—you know it’s painful, but you crave it anyway.

Final Verdict: 7.5/10

Yes, it’s frustrating. Yes, it’s chaotic. Yes, you’ll curse the day you ever queued for free-for-all. But you’ll also laugh, yell, and shout “LET’S GOOOO!” at 2 a.m. when you clutch a stock with one HP left. Brawlhalla is a dumpster fire wrapped in a party game—and somehow, I love it for that.

review:
Unbalanced meta trash that doesn't allow you to play characters you like because they would be just outclassed by other characters. Music is dull, and you turn it off after 10 seconds. The game looks cheap, the characters look like they were made on Flash 20 years ago, and the backgrounds are something that was done in 1 day. Lazy, boring mess that gets old after you've played for a few hours. A game where, despite having dozens of characters, you will see only, like, five of them over and over, because again. Meta.

The only thing this game might be good for is for those drunk nights with friends where you wish to just play some brainless party games to entertain yourselves. And even in this case, downloading an N64 emulator and getting Smash Bros there would be a far more fun way to play something of a similar style. And to think about it. It is actually funny how a game that came out in 1999 actually feels of higher quality in terms of animations, music and especially game mechanics. 

Just don't bother yourself. This game isn't worth your time. And especially your money.

review:
[b]Brawlhalla just didn’t click for me, it felt like a flashy platform fighter that promised depth but landed flat. While I get the appeal, with its cartoonish brawlers and quick matches, the gameplay ended up feeling more chaotic than clever, and that's not really my cup of tea.

The roster is massive and colorful, but it seems like every update just adds more characters instead of fixing the core mechanics. Matches often devolve into button-mashing contests rather than strategic showdowns, and the physics feel inconsistent, sometimes you're pulling off insane aerial combos, and other times your character won’t land a simple hit.

And the community? It’s fine if you're into the competitive grind, but I found it hard to stick around when casual matchups felt unfair and unbalanced. The game is free-to-play with tons of unlocked skins, but there's still a noticeable gap between free players and those who spend on boosters.

In short, Brawlhalla might be a hit for others, but its chaotic combat and focus on cosmetics really didn’t win me over. Definitely not my style of fighter.[/b]

review:
Highly Recommended
✅ (Been playing since near launch)
Posted June 2025

Brawlhalla is honestly one of my favorite beat 'em up games of all time. I started playing around the time it first launched, and even back then—when there were barely any characters—it was a blast.

Despite having fewer attack inputs compared to something like Super Smash Bros., the gameplay felt tight, fast, and incredibly balanced. What really impressed me was how no two matches ever felt the same. Even with a smaller roster early on, the mechanics were strong enough to keep things fresh and fun.

It’s the kind of game that’s easy to pick up, but with enough depth to stick around. Whether you’re playing casually or going sweaty in ranked, Brawlhalla holds up.

review:
This is THE WORST game I've ever laid my eyes upon. The unfathomable amount of SWEATS in this game is ridiculous. This game was made as an attempt to provoke the most amount of rage a human could possibly feel. On top of that, you CANNOT have fun in this game.

The moment your game starts your opponent immediately starts spamming sigs like their life is at stake, but don't you worry, those sigs are unpunishable, so even if they miss it doesn't matter, there's nothing you can do about it anyways.

In the few games you don't get continuously spammed by sigs your opponent will read your every dodge like Doctor Strange and hold you in a combo so long your grandchildren are born before the combo ends.

Every time they add a new character to the game it's like they're deliberately trying their best to ruin everyone's experience when facing off against them.

It doesn't matter how much you practice movement, dodging or anything at all, because at the end of the day when you queue up with real players you're not going to be prepared for the incredible lack of skill and yet the incomprehensible amount of LUCK some players posses.

Stay away from this game if you value the objects closest to you.

review:
Balanced and fun competitive game with a lot of skill expression.

As with many fighting games, it's not very beginner-friendly, and I highly recommend watching a brief video on weapon combos/strings since they are actually pretty easy to learn. Plenty of people complain about sig spamming and broken weapons, and I agree that for beginners, dealing with sigs can be very frustrating. However, I consider the game to be pretty well balanced overall. Every character and every weapon is viable, and although some may be stronger than others at certain times, the devs consistently push out balance patches to try to make it fair. There's also enough skill expression such that there's always an opportunity to outplay your opponent.

Please fix the mac client though, it's unplayable with constant frame dips.

review:
Brawlhalla stands as an enticing entry in the free-to-play fighting game arena, offering a refreshing, accessible take on the platform fighter genre. Its vibrant art style, diverse roster of "Legends" (characters), and intuitive two-button attack system make it incredibly easy to pick up and play for an hour or an evening. The game truly shines in its fast-paced, chaotic glory, especially when bouncing around with friends in casual modes. There's a genuine thrill in landing a devastating string of attacks, spiking an opponent off the stage, or pulling off a clutch recovery. For a game that costs nothing to download, Brawlhalla delivers undeniable moments of pure, unadulterated fun.

However, Brawlhalla's gleaming facade can quickly crack, revealing a core frustration that has plagued its community for years: the prevalence of arguably 'spammy' and overwhelmingly dominant weapon types, most notoriously the Lance.

The Lance, in particular, often transforms what should be a delightful brawl into a maddening exercise in futility. Its incredibly long-reaching, swift, and often juggle-heavy attacks can feel less like a skilled opponent outmaneuvering you and more like an unavoidable, relentless assault. While every weapon has its strengths and weaknesses, the Lance often feels disproportionately rewarded for what appears to be repetitive, low-effort inputs. You'll find yourself on the receiving end of what feels like an endless chain of dash attacks, aerials, and side-airs, leaving you bouncing uncontrollably across the stage with little room to retaliate or even breathe.

It's not just the Lance; other weapons like the Axe and Greatsword, when wielded by players focused solely on repeatedly executing their most effective (and often safest) combos, can induce a similar sense of helplessness. This isn't about tactical defeat where you acknowledge a superior player; it's about the soul-crushing sensation of being completely overwhelmed, experiencing what many frustrated players bluntly describe as being "gimped" or "raped" by a character's often low-effort, high-reward attack patterns. The joy of the fight evaporates, replaced by a bitter sense of exploitation as your stocks vanish, leaving you feeling less outplayed and more just... abused.

In essence, Brawlhalla is a fantastic time when its core mechanics lead to varied, strategic, and engaging combat. But that enjoyment comes with a significant asterisk. It's incredibly fun when you're duking it out with opponents who use their full kit, adapt, and create interesting exchanges. It's dramatically less so when you're on the receiving end of a relentless barrage from a Lance or other similarly aggressive, 'spammy' characters, leaving you feeling more like a punching bag than a participant in a fair fight. If you can stomach that particular flavor of frustration, there's a lot to love, but be warned: your fun is highly conditional on who you're matched against.

Brawlhalla is my instant-launch “one more set” fighter. Pull off a gravity-cancel string with Wu Shang, smile, log off. I crave deeper world stakes, but for a free platform brawler this is hard to beat.

review:
THE ULTIMATE REVENGE ARC

My friends invited me to play Brawlhalla.
I thought, “Oh cool, free game. Probably some fun party vibes.”

I picked a character with a sword. I don’t even remember who.
They told me to press buttons. I did.
They didn’t.

They juggled me. Threw me off the map. Taunted.
One of them said, “Skill issue.”
Another changed their name mid-game to “EZClapVaibhav" 

I was humiliated.

That night I didn’t sleep.
I watched combos on YouTube. I trained in the lab.
I studied movement tech like it was the SAT.
I downloaded finger-stretching exercises.
I mained Mordex.

Two weeks later, I invited them for a rematch.

They laughed.
They shouldn’t have.

First stock? Gone in 14 seconds.
Second stock? Zero-to-death with side light reads.
Final stock? I didn’t even move. I just threw my weapon and taunted.

I didn’t just beat them.
I emotionally destabilized them.

They haven’t logged on since.

Now strangers message me “pls 1v1.”
I say nothing. I just queue.

Brawlhalla didn’t just change me.
It awakened me.

review:
I’ve sunk more hours into Brawlhalla than I’m proud to admit—and I regret none of it. Unlike most fighters out there, this game doesn’t overwhelm you with fancy mechanics or pay-to-win nonsense. It’s raw, fast-paced, and addictive in the best way. Matches are short but intense, and the satisfaction of landing a perfect dodge into a KO? Unmatched.

What keeps me coming back is the character variety and community vibe. There’s a legend for every playstyle, and mastering them feels genuinely rewarding. Whether it’s ranked rage or casual chaos, I’m always feeling something. Most games get stale after a while, but with frequent updates, seasonal events, and straight-up good design, Brawlhalla hasn’t lost its grip on me.

Compared to other platform fighters, Brawlhalla just gets me. It doesn’t try too hard—it just delivers. No flashy cinematics or unnecessary frills. Just pure gameplay, clutch moments, and hype. If you're debating downloading it, do it. But fair warning: you might not stop.

👍 Would recommend. Would rage. Would still come back for more.

review:
This game is ass. This is the most frustrating game ever, and I do not know why you would prefer this over Super Smash Bros or Rivals of Aether, besides this being "free-to-play". The movesets are so god awful, every character begins with the same movesets before you get your weapon. After you get your weapon, you get a moveset which you share with a bunch of other characters besides your down special, neutral special, and side special. Every character has two weapons that they can use, but they are stupidly more powerful than if you don't have a weapon, which makes armed vs. unarmed the equivalent to hydrogen bomb vs. coughing baby. The movement is kind of meh, as you do have dashes and airdodges.  It's also a bit faster than regular platform fighters, but that does not make up the lack of real movesets. Additionally, true combos are very rare in the game, and the ones you do find are very short and lacklustre.

I also put "free-to-play" in quotes because all of the interesting "characters", which are just skins, are locked behind microtransactions. It has fantastic crossovers with Street Fighter, Tekken, Spongebob, Star Wars, etc. However, you will be stuck with the regular characters unless you pay Ubisoft with your hard-earned money.

I really did try to enjoy this game, but I unfortunately couldn't due to the constant problems that I discovered, one after another. The amount of players this game gets surprised me.

review: Take everything good about smash bros and throw it out the window, take everything fun about the movement of platformer games and throw it out the window, and take the creativity of fighting game movesets out of the window. This is how you get brawlhalla. You'd be happier playing smash or mario or street fighter or anything else but instead you're stuck with this. look at yourself in the mirror and realize "have I really fallen this low? Would I go out to eat and actively choose a shit meal over a good one? Why am I commiting a form of self harm and telling myself I enjoy it?" and once you realize this you will never go back. This game is a transition period in peoples lives where they either learn to better themselves or learn to get better at brawlhalla. Only one of those choices comes with long term happiness and satisfaction. Also none of this applies to you if you have no social life. If you are a loser and you know that and you are proud by all means, have at it.

review:
Why does it feel awful to hit anything in this game? Like, I've been playing fighting games since I got squirted out my mothers womb, and only when I played Soulcalibur 4 on XBOX Live with red bars did I get horrible hit detection.

I tried to open a private room and fight with AI, no, the game is like that. The hit detection works fine. It's just that the hit boxes spawn very late with heavy attacks, and they're very small for quick attacks. Also they last for a couple of frames, if that. So I have to anticipate as if there was a massive amount of lag. That's just how this game works.

I hate it. I genuinely thought either my internet was malfunctioning, or I was having a stroke. This game is not for me - is the best thing I can say about it.

review: Brawlhalla. I have experienced more desk slamming rage in this game than almost any other. (Except overwatch that game stole 3,000 hours of my life and should condemned to hell) despite this intense anger each day I start it up and play again. This is the platform fighter for anyone who wants a highly competitive skill based game. In lower ranks you’ll want to claw your eyes out as you get spammed and absolutely dominated by certain weapons or abilities. While balancing does have a part to play these tactics can easily be outplayed by investing just a little bit of time into actually developing your skill at the base mechanics. I have sunk 700 hours and at least a 1,000 dollars into this game and I will continue to. Play with friends or descend into the burning hell of the ranked ladder and you will have fun. It’s all worth it for when you finally hit that one combo or hit every dodge read on a higher ranked player. I recommend this game if you are looking for an extremely competitive experience. Otherwise go play smash or something.

review:
In general a good game. 
Positives:
If you play it with friends, you can have the fun of your life.
It is the best fighting platfomer on pc. 
The thing that kept me hooked was that you can learn a weapon an then pick up almost every legend with it. After that you have a solid stable on learning new weapons.
The game has satisfying combo gameplay if you play combo weapons.
It has good balancing in general, so that you can play anything you want and have success with it.

Negatives:
If you hop into experimental(Unranked 1v1) you are just matched with 12 year old kids that are sweating their a** of or toxic people. Dont even get me started on enemys that are just spamming one move (not sig spamming) or playing passive af. 
There is nothing like a chill session of Brawl if you are not high elo and know everything about the game.
Monitisation was good until they added bundels and sidekicks imo.

In general i would recommend the game, because the moments you can have with your friends (and with the game in general) outweigh the neagtives

review:
If hell had a Wi-Fi connection and a roster of bootleg Smash Bros. rejects, Brawlhalla would be its main attraction. This game isn’t just broken—it’s a godforsaken glitchy clown fiesta where skill goes to die and button mashers reign supreme.

Let’s start with the characters. Every single one feels like they were designed during a caffeine crash at 4 a.m. They’re either overpowered gremlins with weapons that track your soul, or pathetic noodles who swing like they’ve never held an object in their life. Don’t get me started on that sword spammer who just hits side-light, side-air like it's a holy ritual. Playing against some of these losers feels like getting slapped repeatedly with a wet sock full of salt.

The balance? Non-existent. Either you’re juggling someone to the moon with three buttons or getting hit with a 25-hit unpunishable combo that started from a toe tap. The devs seem to balance the game by spinning a wheel and saying “Yeah, let’s buff that guy again for no reason.” Legends rotate from “god tier” to “literal trash” on a weekly basis.

And the servers—Jesus H. Combo-Locked Christ. You either teleport around like a Dragon Ball Z character on meth or you lag into oblivion and die off-stage like some tragic Shakespearean glitch.

I’ve seen IKEA furniture held together with tears and duct tape run smoother than Brawlhalla’s netcode. Playing ranked in this game feels like doing brain surgery with a chainsaw in a hurricane.

Matchmaking? It pairs you with platinum smurfs who’ve mained Mordex since 2012 and treat every match like it’s the Brawlhalla Olympics. Oh, and let’s not forget the community—half are sweaty emote-spamming gremlins and the other half are 12-year-olds who think spamming taunts after every kill is a personality trait.

To sum it up:

Trash balance

Garbage servers

Brain-dead characters

Rage-inducing mechanics

Community toxicity levels that make League of Legends look like a meditation retreat

This game isn’t just bad. It’s a cosmic joke wrapped in lag, sprinkled with toxic sweat, and sold to us like it’s supposed to be fun.

Uninstalling this pixelated rage simulator before I throw my monitor out the window.

review: You're considering this game because you like playing smash with your friends and online, right? Think again. You know that one friend who's an absolute sweat and knows that one Bayonetta combo that instantly kills you? 85% of people in casual matches are that person. Ranked is even worse. If you're lucky, you'll get some good matches on occasion. My character recommendation is the furry bird, no one plays her and her moves are pretty good, at least for a casual player. If you're going against the sweats you're cooked as most characters because you don't have a shield button like in smash. There's no shield. At all. No stopping the equivalent to Metaknight's side-B. This entire game would be fixed if they simply added that. That being said, I did humiliate a twitch streamer who was a sweat the other day, so it can be fun at times. I joined their stream and they were banging on their table :3 7.5/10 would reccomend because the game is fun overall, they should just force people who are sweats to play in ranked.

review:
I really need to get this off my chest. When I first played this on a small computer, I really liked the game. But I couldn't play more because the computer wasn't strong enough to keep playing. So years later, when I managed to get a Steam Deck, I've been playing it since. There were these crossovers and events and battle passes that got me playing it more, but I didn't realize how cruel the monetization was. Also, I didn't realize that Ubisoft owned the game. The company has had bad reputation with how they manage their games lately, especially the Rayman series. The monetization on the recent event made me realize; enough is enough. I let myself be fooled by these kinds of things, such as free-to-play games. I've learned my lesson after playing MultiVersus.

I just have one thing to say: "Say NO to free-to-play games!"

review:
How can you possibly ruin the gameplay of a FLASH GAME???
Imagine creating a FIGHTING game with INPUT issues - enter brawlhalla.
The game itself is good, but the chances are that it wont even run smooth on your device, because for the love of GOD, the players SHOULD NOT go through 7 layers of hell to try and optimize the launch options/graphics option just for it to play somewhat decent. The devs release insanely expensive skins without giving the server/bugs side of the game little to no attention. A lot of issues were coming from Easy anti-cheat, but it was apparently embedded within, so no option to disable it now. The game felt better when tech-test and framefixunbounded were an option.
Now in my situation, having a relatively good setup and still experiencing LAG (not server-side) is crazy, and after 1200+ hours and reaching peak 2100ish I decided to save myself some nerves for the future after:

1)Testing the game with all launch option avalable - no result
2)Changing every parameter in nvidia graphics driver menu (literally every option) - no result
3)Limiting fps to match screen hz or double that, trying with v-sync - no result
4)Easily getting 300 fps with little to no cpu load, but still experiencing stutter and dropped inputs
5)Giving up on dashjumping because the character wont fast-fall/ register dashes/ dashing too late/ not jumping
6)Testing the keyboard and resetting the settings - keyboard is fine
7)Recording the gameplay with key press tracker overlay - all the keys are pressed as intended - no action/dropped/latency on input
8)Playing with controller - same issues
9)Dying off screen because character wont jump
10)Reintalling windows wont help, and having high speed LAN probably wont help too unless you are on wifi - the game itself is diying from lack of care from devs. 

And I am not talking about balance issues, but thats another story since ill probably get eaten alive by sweats and kids saying "skill issue" (you are welcome to say it in replies as long as they help my review get pushed)

review:
I really hope this review actually gets seen because you shouldn't let the 80% positive reviews fool you, this game isn't good at all. I have well over 1500 hours (PC+PS4) in this rabbit hole and nothing has ever changed. 

At first you play the game, get confused by what it's happening with the amount of options you have (surprised how they haven't slapped a "buy this beginners bundle for a free legend" in your face when you open the game) and after finally picking a game mode to play, not like there's any creative difference between them, you pick a legend based either on how they look or their weapons. Beginners mistake, this will either make you quit on the spot because your weapon is too complicated to be used or you're going to spam that character till you find out that you can also use light attacks.  This is brawlhalla.

This game's ranked mode is a complete joke. You can play and rank up, as much as you want - if you're not diamond be ready to be sig spammed from earth to actually seeing fucking valhalla in real life. You pick the character you grinded 3 weeks to unlock, confidant you're not that bad with them because you saw 2 tutorials on youtube and the next 10 games you'll play (if you manage to do 10 without ragging) will be people that really have nothing better to do than click on the heavy attack button. You're off stage? heavy. Weaponless? heavy or run till they get one. White, yellow, orange or red? Heavy. And not to mention how some of these character sigs are extremely hard to punish and even if you do learn how to punish sigs, if you don't punish the enemy with lightning speed then you'll go for round 2 of sigs that are faster than flash himself.

The shop on this game is also completely pathetic, you can spend money on: Skins, weapon skins, podiums, sidekicks, chests that go up to 50 bucks if you want to  get the 3 special skins (rng way to get skins either cheaper or exclusive skins) , trail effects (not for when you walk/dash but for when your sig hits the enemy and will kill them), pets that will follow you???, emotes, crossovers and, obviously, the battle pass. There's so many things you can buy that it makes me wonder if they just quit trying to make a game and now are just making a cash grab.

This games balancing is probably the biggest joke tho. Characters that will kill you in 4 attacks, characters that MIGHT kill you after throwing you around 50 times, character stats completely broken and not balanced at all, sigs that cover the entire stage or that will go down if you use them at the corner of the stage. It's just hilarious how they keep doing it and ignore the complains of the entire community.

If YOU are looking for a game that wants to make you feel like you're going to overdose this is for you - either that or you have nerves of steel. Even with friends if you decide to play 2v2's this game feels like a 9 to 5 job, worse than any gacha game you could ever play. Almost forgot to mention that if you have a cheap keyboard and plan on actually learning the game be ready to spend 100+ euros on a EZ keyboard or a Wooting, else you're going nowhere with how bad this games inputs work.

Bmg needs to fix all of their issues with the game. Brawlhalla has low requirements till you actually open the game. As soon as you open the shop your game WILL lag, you fps will drop in the character select screen and at the start of every game, issues that have been a problem for multiple years now (unless your pc costed anything between 2000 and 5000$, yes, this game CAN lag on your ryzen 7 5600x and 3070 ti.)

Horrific game, I only keep coming back to it because i genuinely like brawlhalla. I hope BMG stops pretending they have a good game and they actually fix the problems this game has, I'd love to see this game get more love and attention besides 40K people watching the e-sports for free items like skins/colors/weapons skins.

review:
This game is a fun and free way to use your small existence living in a blind rage. I enjoy grinding through the low ranks against the many different characters BMG has added to the game that make it more and more broken every single year. I enjoy getting to diamond and going against the 10,000th Mordex and Nix main in a row with over 5,000 hours on just the scythe. 

The emojis are so extremely toxic and BMG says go on! Toxicity is rampant in this game and the devs promote and even incentivize you to be toxic, so don't take it to hard when the sig spammer orion hits the skele-griddy on you. Also when that ex valhallan Mirage gets angry after you wipe them, adds you to a private lobby and tells you to end it all, the game goes from a 7 to a 10. You can feel the rage in their tiny little scythe hands.

People blame ubisoft for brawlhallas gross and predatory marketing strategies, but tell me, do you think the CEO and other lizards of BMG are upset about making another $40 off a 1400 elo Wu Shang die hard? HECK NO THEY AINT!  This game is just going to get worse and worse with its prices. Maybe well even be lucky to get a discount code to join a match!

This game is much more stable on the internet then smash and that's a huge reason why I love it. I wanted a smash like game where I didn't phase through the map if my internet stuttered for 0.1 seconds in a rain storm and this is it. 

You will rage. You will hate yourself and all of humanity for being able to create this game, but if you stick with it, you just might beat that 10k hour snordex <3.

***ALSO FOR THE SWEET LOVE OF GOD, NEVER EVER BUY THE ALL LEGENDS PACK. CHARACTERS ARE THE MAIN THING YOU BUY WITH GOLD YOU GET FOR FREE, AFTER YOU'VE UNLOCKED ALL THE LEGENDS YOU WILL HAVE LIKE 500K GOLD***

3400 hours on steam alone. 800 more hours on console. The appeal to this game is really only the competitive aspect. If you are the type of person who plays games to enjoy them, don't play this game. If you play games to improve then maybe you'll like brawl. However the balance and esports teams for BMG are severely understaffed so don't expect any balance changes any time soon. BMG won't listen to your complaints and will instead focus on making $40 skins rather than improving the game. review:
[h1]This game makes 0 sense[/h1]

So i play this game for a while even if my time says otherwise, since i played it on my ps4 before coming to the pc and this game as some serious problems. Me and my friend are playing ranked to try and get the best we can but let me say a few reasons why this game sucks that we saw while playing.

[i][b]The matchmaking[/b][/i] - its complete trash, we can have 5 guys in a row that have no idea what they are doing, then have a duo and one being AFK and after all that we find people that dont touch grass or know what that is. And I am getting diamond's that i already lost with on the base of gold, i literally got into gold and i am getting idiots like these.

[i]Bugged sounds[/i] - while playing we noticed multiple times where the sound of grabbing a weapon or a bomb would play and then we find ourselves without anything in hand. But this bug didnt affect only weapons it affected hit sounds too, where we would hear an enemy get hit and then nothing has happaned to him.

[i]Throwable not working[/i] - a bunch of times when i am falling down i throw my weapon to damage the enemy so he cant hit me, but for no reason there are times where the weapon just phases through the enemy so i just get hit by him and die. [b]Even better when the weapon goes through the enemy and hits my friend[/b]

[i]Invicibility?[/i] - we hit the enemy, there is sound and their bar changes color but they dont get any knockback.

[i]Hit and grab[/i] - the enemy is in a middle of taking a combo and still somehow he is able to grab a weapon.

[i]The order of attack doesnt make sense[/i] - unless someone can tell me why a normal punch has advantage over a spear i dont think this makes sense at all, not to mention certain attacks should advantage over others since why would a boot have advantage in charging against a spear charge? And lastly why a big rolling rock, Kor, doesnt have any immunity against a bunch of attacks, like at least some type of immunity.

[i]A tutorial please[/i] - most of the daily quests are easy to follow, but come on there are some that you literally need to go to [insert your favorite browser here] and search in how to do it. How would i know what a backwards signature KO?

[i]Quest Guide[/i] - yes another problem with the quests, there should be a possibility to pin the quest you want to do in the corner of the screen so you know if you did it or not.

[i]Physic's is not feeling well[/i] - so a guy was in a bubble, i clearly hit him from the bottom right corner with a heavy lance and he went flying to the top left corner right? after all he had his healh on red already. No, he for no reason just flew a bit and full left for no reason.

[i]Dance Party[/i] - so is this a fighting game or a dacing one? because i swear i only see idiots jumping like they are dancing like an idiot and then they just die because who would have guess that DANCING IN A BATTLE WOULDNT DO ANYTHING IN A FIGHT.

[i]Take those gravity things out[/i] - i played in a time where that stupid gravity thing wasnt a thing and i swear i miss that. back then you had a mode where you played with or without that, put that again because that is super SUPER annoying.

[i]Is there any dodges or did they get removed?[/i] - so did i lose an update where they removed the dodge? because it never happens to me. or maybe its a 1 in 1000000 chance?

[i]No bubble?[/i] - so a guy was clearly put in a bubble, the bubble appeared for a fraction of a second and then nothing happaned at all, the bubble vanished. and no, no one hit him while in the bubble.

[i]Massive Legs[/i] - why the hell the breakdance attack has such a long range, its just disarmed attack makes no sense.

[i]No Vehicles Allowed[/i] - do tell me, who in the right mind thought having Red Raptor have a attack that covers the entire arena was a good idea?

[i]Great Plataform[/i] - so my friend clearly landed on the plataform but for some reason he goes from it for no reason, no logic. The shadow was clearly on top of it too.

I will be adding more here if i find more stupid stuff.

review: Brawlhalla is like a chaotic family reunion where everyone settles arguments by punching each other off floating platforms… and somehow it’s fun. It’s a free-to-play platform fighter with a colorful roster of legends, from sword-wielding knights to kung fu frogs (okay, maybe not frogs, but it feels like there should be). Matches are fast, silly, and full of “oops” moments — like when you try a heroic leap and just yeet yourself into the abyss. The controls are easy to learn, but the mind games and combos can get deep, especially when you’re trying to dodge that one guy who’s clearly been playing since the dawn of time. Whether you’re brawling online, with friends, or against bots, it’s pure, ridiculous fun.

review:
Brawlhalla can be extremely fun and satisfying to play, but it is ultimately an inherently flawed, deeply unbalanced, terribly optimized, and lazily-made game. These are objective game-breaking issues, many of which have been present for 8 years now. (903 hours at time of review, level 93 Ember, 1748 ELO) 

-Lag:
 Even when the proper server is selected, you will frequently face debilitating lag and 'rubber-banding' in online matches. But here's the real kicker: the lag ISN'T just from the network. Astonishingly, this 2D game will oftentimes lag while in the client-side MENUS.  

-Egregious Hitboxes and Hurtboxes:
Even though this is a 2D, sprite-based game, and it would be elementary to have pixel-perfect hitboxes, this is not the case. The result is that many attack-animations are physically larger than their own effective-range, creating frustrating moments where an attack visibly strikes an opponent, but deals no damage. The inverse is equally a problem. I oftentimes will hit opponents with an attack and will feel cheated on their behalf, because this is a huge issue.

-Ambiguous Animations: 
Unfortunately, the R3T4RDs who develop this game have never heard of the concept of "telegraphing" in martial-arts. The consequence of this is that every time a new legend is released (literally monthly) you will be helpless against that new legend until you have manually memorized all of their different attack animations. Very often legends will have signature moves which are completely ambiguous as to where the hurtbox is actually going until the frame where the damage is dealt. 

The post-match screen:
Literally with each passing year since this game's initial release they have continually ADDED to the amount of junk and nonsense that you have to sit/skip your way through at the end of each match. When this game came-out, you could end a match and start another in just a few seconds. Today, it is so bloated that its almost laughable. It's such a shameless insult to your player's intelligence to literally force them to sit there and watch a virtual wheel spin as to determine which cosmetic item they will unlock. Even when I spam the C button, sometimes I have to skip through so many artificial XP bars and unlockable screens that Im slapping the "C" key for upwards of 15 seconds just to get back to the actual game. It is insane. 

Balance: 
As of writing this, Brawlhalla has 66 unique legends. Despite this, once you reach an ELO of 1700 or higher, you will almost exclusively be fighting the same 10-12 legends over-and-over. This game is blatantly unbalanced, and many newer legends and weapons effectively make swaths of the roster uncompetitive/unplayable. 

Random Changes and Nerfs: 
For how deeply broken and unbalanced this game is, the spotty, half-hearted, and seemingly random changes that the developers DO make end up causing more harm than good. Things like nerfing weapon throws, having 1v1 ranked matches where you randomly START with your secondary weapon, it all seems so aimless. 


Unfortunately, Brawlhalla is a good game about 70% of the time, and in those rare moments when its running buttery-smooth and you're having fun, it can really scratch a certain itch. But sooner rather than later, you'll find yourself feeling cheated by the experience, and you're better-off not playing it at-all.

review:
I consider this a pretty hard pass. I walked into this hoping it'd be a casual-ish smash bros clone, but it's far from casual. 

Admittedly, I'm not much of a fighting game expert, so this game isn't exactly in my wheelhouse, but from what little I played I was constantly getting curb-stomped. In 1v1 matches, I was constantly combo'd to death without having a chance to get my footing. I'm not interested in playing a game where I get to be someone else's punching bag - that's what a job's for, after all.

Note, I was seeing this in both ranked & unranked matches. Sure, I expected this in ranked, but not at my ranking. I played enough placement matches to earn high bronze, then worked my way up to low silver - and yet I'd still get matched against players who seemed to be experts at the game. Maybe my expectations were in the wrong, but still...

Moving on though.

Another issue this game has is poor performance. In fact lagginess is the ultimate reason I'm writing this review. Firstly, when I open up the in-game store, the game tends to lag when trying to load only a handful of animated characters at a time. Which is weird, because those animations are 2D, so they shouldn't be as performance-heavy as trying to animate a 3D model with several bones (and also handle the lighting for all the model's polygons), and yet I've seen better performance in games with more advanced graphics. But the bigger issue is the lag I've seen in matches. There seems to be one map in particular that tries to constantly scroll forward to keep the players on their toes. And that map is laggy as hell for me. It ruined the public match I was just in, and it smothered any hope I had for the game.

One other weird thing I'd like to point out is that the game feels bad to play, and I'm not trying to say my feelings were hurt. A LOT of attacks feel like they should hit but don't for some stupid reason. 

Let me explain.

There are a handful of different weapon types in the game. For example, sword & gun. As you can imagine, each weapon has different characteristics such as the given reach/range, its attack speed & damage. But what gets weird is that some ranged weapons, like a pair of pistols, don't deal damage in a range from the shooter to the target. Instead, they seemingly have an invisible hit-box that sits a small distance in front of the shooter. If the target isn't colliding with the hit-box, then the target isn't hit - even if the target is between the shooter & the hit-box. 

And I really want to stress that this is just a single example. I've had situations where a spear's upward attack didn't connect for the same reasons, and I assume this is a potential issue for all weapons types, not that I bothered playing long enough to figure that out.

TL;DR

Don't bother with this game. It's laggy. It's clunky. The music is pretty shallow & forgettable. The visuals are okay (which is where most of the game's monetization comes from). The matchmaking sucks. 

And if you do want to play it, don't grab the dlcs 'til you've gotten a good look at the game first. You'll thank me later.

review:
At first, Brawlhalla feels like the best party you’ve ever been invited to. Bright colors, chaotic maps, and characters flying across the screen like fireworks—it’s pure joy in motion. You throw out random attacks, accidentally land a combo, and suddenly you feel like a professional esports player. It’s lighthearted, fun, and endlessly replayable.

Then… something changes.

Your opponents stop being silly little cartoon characters and start transforming into omnipotent gods with the reflexes of lightning itself. That Orion across the stage? He’s not just another player, he’s an eldritch being who has calculated your every button press before you even touch the controller. Every weapon you pick up feels like a pool noodle while theirs is a divine hammer forged in the molten heart of a dying star.

And this is where the spiral begins.

Your cheerful “just one more match” becomes “I must ascend past mortality itself to land a single hit.” Every dodge is punished. Every jump is countered. Every stock you lose is another piece of your soul evaporating into the void. The music doesn’t sound playful anymore—it’s a funeral march. The stages don’t look colorful—they’re mocking you, every platform a reminder of your inevitable downfall.

By the tenth loss in a row, you’re no longer playing Brawlhalla. Brawlhalla is playing you. The game devours your hope, your joy, your sanity. The screen flashes “KO!” and you don’t even see it anymore—it’s just another reminder that everything is temporary, fleeting, doomed to collapse into dust.

And yet… the moment the match ends, your finger twitches. You press “Play Again.” Because deep down, you don’t want freedom. You want to burn with the game. To go down swinging in the eternal digital colosseum.

10/10. Would suffer again.

review: This game is unbelievably amazing if your sole purpose in life is to have a sweaty, fat 12-year-old plow their scythe up your anal cavity and rip out all vital organs. Brawhalla's vast range of unique combos and weapons exhibits such robust creativity to the extent that players only require two brain cells to be godly in this game! Furthermore, Brawhalla’s community is truly the pinnacle of gaming culture, where many players demonstrate good sportsmanship through a variety of fun emojis! And occasionally, players wish to further connect by inviting you to custom lobbies, to enact thoughtful exchanges with one another! I am starting to lose count of the amount of times I have been told to kill myself!! This game’s only made me break two monitors! Only two!! If that’s not considered a steal, then I don’t know what is! Another positive aspect I feel is overlooked is its mysterious attributes. I will never know the degree of skill my opponent is going to have despite the claimed “accuracy” of ELO rating! Hell, I was at 1965 and plummeted back to gold! And I still got paired with Diamond Ranks! This obscure inconsistency adds a whole new excitement as I do not know what the ♥♥♥♥ I am going to do to myself after a match! I am very appreciative of the experience Brawhalla has provided me, as it has excavated whole new emotions that I had yet to discover. To summarize, if you’re looking for that extra push to jump off that cliff or bridge, then this is the game for you!

review:
Brawlhalla is hands down one of my favorite games. It blends fast-paced combat with beautifully stylized graphics and smooth animations that make every match feel alive. The character designs are diverse and charming, and the stages are vibrant without being distracting.

What truly sets Brawlhalla apart is its combo system—tight, responsive, and rewarding for players who take the time to master it. Every weapon feels unique, and learning how to counter different playstyles adds depth to the experience. But beware: if you’re not skilled enough, escaping from pro players is nearly impossible. The skill ceiling is high, and that’s exactly what makes it so addictive.

And me, yo boy playing as Daisy and manages to get that W at the end while having to go through a lot. I started being broke as hell, hitting unlucky spaces, minigame fumbles and having to battle against my brother and Toad. So I won, my brother 2nd, my friend 3rd and Toad, the homie gave it all he got but at the end, completely destroyed him putting him in dead last. Ong play this game with your friends cause in Mario Party, Anything can happen.

If i've learned anything from this game, is that Toad aint givin up on his closest rivals as he always gets back up, no matter how many times he has fallen.

review:
Brawlhalla, despite being one of the most popular free-to-play platform fighters, has earned a reputation among many players for being frustrating to play. The core issue doesn’t lie in the graphics, mechanics, or roster of characters, but in the way the game’s design encourages certain playstyles. One of the biggest complaints is that players often spend most of the match running, jumping, and avoiding fights, only engaging in combat when it benefits them. This creates a gameplay environment that feels unfair, uncompetitive, and, ultimately, unenjoyable.

First, the movement system in Brawlhalla is extremely flexible. Players can chain dodges, jumps, and recoveries to stay airborne or keep distance almost indefinitely. While this mobility is impressive from a technical standpoint, it has the side effect of enabling extremely passive play. Instead of clashing head-on and testing skill, many players abuse the movement system to waste time and avoid taking risks.

Second, the scoring and damage systems reward this style of play. In most matches, it is advantageous to avoid fights until an opponent is already weakened, then swoop in to finish them off. This creates a “vulture” effect where players only fight when they know they can secure a knockout. As a result, genuine combat exchanges are rare, and matches often devolve into long periods of dodging followed by quick, opportunistic attacks.

Third, this behavior erodes the competitive spirit of the game. Fighting games are supposed to reward precision, timing, and skill in direct combat. But in Brawlhalla, those who want to fight aggressively are often punished by losing stocks faster, while the players who avoid conflict and play passively end up gaining the advantage. This flips the usual competitive dynamic on its head, making the game feel less about fighting and more about who can be the most annoying at avoiding conflict.

In conclusion, Brawlhalla has strong fundamentals as a fighting game, but its mechanics encourage a frustrating meta where players run, jump, and only engage when it benefits them. This passive playstyle makes the game feel “dogshit” to many players, because it robs matches of their intensity and fun. Until the developers address these design issues, the game will continue to suffer from a reputation of being more about running away than actually fighting.

review:
Дешёвая пародия
Жила была super smash bros и не тужила.. И резко появились инди энтузиасты которые на коленке склепали простую по задумке и механику игру. Анимации в игре очень дешманские, но не смотря на это смогла привлечь людей огромным количеством доната и рейтингом, конечно же (ну и привлекла электроник артс, но я уже не знаю как так получилось поэтому сказать про это не могу). Естественно на донат можно закрыть глаза, ибо игра бесплатная а скины ничего не дадут, не изменят. Но то во что сейчас (в 2024 году) превращается игра это не совсем хорошо. Персонажей добавляют и делают их всё более простыми (характеристики отличные, атаки до ужаса быстрые и идеально подходят для спама), таким образом чем легче персонаж тем лучше будет играться новичкам. Игры вымирает, но очень медленно.. Впрочем как и все игры в какой то период. Конечно как бесплатная альтернатива это великолепно, с другом поиграть прикольно. Но на постоянную игру вечером я бы посоветовал купить файтинг поинтересней. Что бы не казаться голословным скажу что у меня 1000 часов и я на самом деле не особо жалею. А также забыл добавить что есть режим тренировки, там можно опробовать любого персонажа/скин/кроссовер - это круто =)

Доступность
Большой онлайн
Уникальные механики. Много режимов и в целом функций
Огромные деньги в киберспорте. И разных матчей очень много даже сейчас (в 2024г.)
Совместимость игры, оптимизация. Тут и добавить нечего, тянуло на старом ноуте. И весит меньше гигабайта (можно быстро скачать поиграть и удалить)
Как бы странно не звучало это одна из самых сбалансированных игр, может просто файтингов. Игру всё ещё обновляют, и оружия остаются умеренными против любого другого. Единственное реально отличие персонажей это их характеристики, всё.
Дешёвая анимация, рисовка
Бравлхалла заставляет играть больше тем что бы купить лишь одного персонажа.. иногда это бывает долго и скучно, в основном для новичков
Если в игре есть баланс персонажей, то баланс поиска игр почти полностью отсутствует. В рейтинге попадаются те к кому ты ещё не готов, причём почти всегда. Единственное место где играют в основном новичковости это обычные матчи 2v2 или 1v1 (где выбирается 3 легенды). Но обычные матчи я не буду осуждать потому что это глупо тк там могут быть и сандстормы и новичковости.. если хотите по настоящему чему то научится смотрите повторы своих игр в экспериментальных матчах (режим такой)
Токсичность.. Наверное главный минус и причина выхода большинства знатоков. Возможно раньше комьюнити было чуточку лучше, но я не уверен.. Как любая игра с рейтингом тут есть ужасные и злые люди, но тут их по какой то причине намного больше, что странно для детской игры. Если новички относятся к поражению с добротой то люди кто играет уже много в 50% случаев реальные токсики.. к сожалению.

review:
After spending over 1,000 hours in Brawlhalla, I can confidently say this game is the definition of “easy to learn, hard to master.”

Every legend feels like a new way to express yourself, but the real addiction is the endless mind games — predicting dodges, punishing bad habits, and pulling off a crazy edge-guard that makes you feel like a genius.

The community? Chaotic, salty, hilarious, but somehow that’s part of the charm. Ranked will humble you, customs will make you laugh, and 2v2s will ruin friendships in the best way possible.

Is it perfect? No. The balance changes sometimes feel like the devs are trolling us, and you’ll definitely meet a few spammers who seem to have one button on their keyboard. But that’s Brawlhalla: it’s messy, it’s competitive, and it’s ridiculously fun.

Would I recommend it after 1,000 hours? Absolutely. Just prepare yourself for the most intense platform fighter experience you can get for free.

10/10 would lose elo again.

review:
genuinely do not play this game if you're trying to have fun. 

not only do the devs refuse to implement common sense features like being able to turn off crossovers/skins, mute weapon skins that have obnoxious sounds, or create an unranked gamemode to play with competitive rules (they force you to either play ranked or play friendlies where you can't hit your teammate and you can fucking pick up bombs to throw)..

but they also just literally do not give a single fuck about any player other than pro players. orb or whatever weapon bad for 99.99% of the playerbase? too bad they're nerfing it because one single dude who's insane at the game played it in the most recent tournament and ended up winning. and to make matters worse the nerfs almost always end up being nerfs that barely matter for anyone power wise but just make the weapon feel more sluggish and clunky.

oh and let's not forget the part where quests for events and such can either be as simple as "knock people out" or "do xyz random obscure action that the devs made up a word for and wont actually tell you what to do and oh a new probably cant do it anyways lol" and even if you try 9/10 times you're going to queue some sweaty ass loser in friendlies who hasn't seen daylight in a week. 90% of that "skill" gap too is that they spent hours and hours learning to do obscure and stupid as hell inputs like short dash jumping or play insanely passively because the game rewards you for doing so.

so once again.. genuinely stay away from this game if you care about having fun. the devs couldn't care less about you, the community is overly toxic despite being small and the game it's self feels like it's basically built from the ground up to screw over anyone who's new to it. like seriously play any other game don't help keep this game from dying.

review:
I’ve been playing Brawlhalla since I was a kid, and it’s hard to put into words how much this game has meant to me. It wasn’t just a fighting game.. it was a part of my life. I played it with my best friends, cousins, my brother, and even with girls I was dating lol. It became a ritual, a bonding activity, and a source of laughter, competition, and countless memories.

What I love most about Brawlhalla is its simplicity. You can pick it up in a few minutes, but mastering it takes years. The mechanics are easy to understand, yet every character feels unique, and the endless combinations of weapons and playstyles kept me hooked. No two matches ever felt the same.

But beyond the gameplay, it was the moments that made it unforgettable.. screaming when someone pulled off a crazy recovery, laughing when a perfectly timed weapon throw ruined everything, or arguing over who really was the “best” among us. It didn’t matter if I was playing on the couch with family or online with friends across the world, Brawlhalla always brought us together.

Looking back, I realize that this game wasn’t just entertainment.. it was a backdrop for relationships, memories, and years of my life. For that, Brawlhalla will always have a special place in my heart.

Final Verdict: 10/10 - Not just a game, but a piece of my story.

review:
🌟 A Free-to-Play Platform Fighter That Shines with Friends and Customization! 🌟

"Brawlhalla" is a free-to-play 2D platform fighting game that has consistently evolved since its 2017 release, offering chaotic fun for up to 8 players locally or online. With full cross-play support across PC, consoles, and mobile, it boasts a massive player base and frequent updates that keep the experience fresh . The game combines accessible controls with deep mechanics, making it easy to pick up but challenging to master.

The core gameplay involves knocking opponents off the stage using a variety of weapons and signature moves, reminiscent of titles like Super Smash Bros. Each of the 66 "Legends" has unique stats, two weapon types, and customizable cosmetics . Modes range from casual free-for-alls and ranked matches to quirky alternatives like Brawlball and Bombsketball . The recent addition of "Ascended Legends" (like Ascended Nix) introduces mythic-tier skins with enhanced visual and audio effects, adding depth to customization .

However, the game has its flaws. Public lobbies can be toxic, especially in ranked modes, and the grind for unlocking Legends or cosmetics might feel slow without purchasing the All Legends Pack ($39.99) . The reliance on RNG for some rewards and the aggressive monetization of Mammoth Coins for premium items may frustrate free players . Additionally, the simplicity of tasks in events like Brawlhalla Fest 2025 can become repetitive over time .

Pros:

🎮 Cross-Platform Play: Seamless multiplayer across PC, console, and mobile .

🎨 Deep Customization: Tons of skins, emotes, and events (e.g., Brawlhalla Fest 2025 with free rewards) .

⚔️ Varied Gameplay: Multiple modes and frequent updates keep things exciting .

🆓 Free to Play: No pay-to-win elements; all characters can be earned through gameplay .

Cons:

🗣️ Toxicity in Public Lobbies: Ranked modes often attract toxic behavior .

💰 Grindy Progression: Unlocking all Legends without paying takes time .

🔁 Repetitive Events: Some missions feel monotonous after a while .

🎲 RNG-Based Rewards: Chests and drops rely heavily on luck .


"Brawlhalla" is a standout platform fighter that excels in social play and customization. While it has issues with toxicity and monetization, its frequent updates, cross-platform support, and sheer content make it a must-try for fans of the genre. Best enjoyed with friends or in custom lobbies!

review:
🛡️ BRAWLHALLA: The Game Where Jumping Off the Map Is a Valid Strategy 🛡️
I downloaded Brawlhalla thinking, “Cool, Smash Bros but free.” What I got was a pixelated coliseum of chaos where Thor can fistfight SpongeBob’s cousin and lose to a sentient toaster with better spacing.
Gameplay?
It’s a platform fighter. You jump, dodge, and yeet your enemies off the stage like it’s a cosmic sumo match. Combos are crisp, movement is buttery, and every match feels like a caffeine-fueled ballet of violence. You’ll spend 30 minutes in training mode learning a 5-hit string, then get bodied by someone spamming side-sig with a smile.
Characters?
• 	Over 50 legends, each with two weapons and a dream.
• 	You’ve got sword-wielding knights, alien wrestlers, anime archers, and a literal cowgirl with a cannon.
• 	Also, crossover madness: Shovel Knight, Adventure Time, Walking Dead, and WWE. Yes, you can suplex someone off a cliff as John Cena.
Weapons?
• 	Blasters? Pew pew.
• 	Scythe? Emotional damage.
• 	Hammer? The embodiment of “I don’t know what I’m doing but it’s working.”
• 	Gauntlets? Punch first, ask questions never.
Ranked Mode?
It’s a spiritual journey. You start in Bronze, full of hope. You reach Gold, full of rage. You hit Diamond, full of existential dread. Every match is a test of patience, reflexes, and whether you can resist typing “gg ez” ironically.
Community?
• 	Half wholesome, half gremlin.
• 	You’ll get complimented for a sick combo, then emoted on for missing a recovery.
• 	The salt mines are deep, but the memes are deeper.
Final Verdict: Brawlhalla is the only game where I’ve rage quit, reinstalled, and queued again in under 60 seconds. It’s fast, fun, and free—with just enough jank to keep it spicy. Whether you’re a sweaty ranked warrior or a casual chaos gremlin, there’s a legend waiting to be your main.
10/10 would get edge-guarded by a 12-year-old again.

[h3] hell even those braindead morons would pick ONE unfair character and that is.. [/h3]

[u] Loki [/u]
i have problem with this character and the weapons he uses, normally im fine with Scythe and Katars but [b] WHO DESIGNED THIS F**K [/b] , his weapon combination is stupid and heavy attacks is so hard to counter, HIS SIDE HEAVY ATTACK STILL HITS YOU EVERYWHERE AND YOU WILL GET DOMINATED IF THE PLAYER ACTIVATED 1 BRAIN CELL, so if loki becomes free to play for a week, you are out of luck because you will meet players like this

[h3] Weapons and Legends balance [/h3]
as a guy who played this game years ago and from my opinion, [b] EVERYTHING [/b] is unbalanced, characters like Imugi and Queen Nai, their Atk and Def stats, is abnormally HIGH, so you will have to risk everything to send the opponent to blast-pit or they will obliterate you if made one mistake. Katars' attack speed is VERY fast, they will pin you down and use heavy attack OR spam it, you know what let's do a small summary, Spears? spam heavy attack, Hammer? spam heavy attack, Bow?? spam heavy attack, OKAY YOU CAN SPAM HEAVY ATTACKS ON EVERY WEAPON, EVERY CHARACTERS AND YOU WILL STILL WIN.

[h3] Brawlhalla is fun but only if the opponent wants to play fair and not spam heavy attacks [/h3]
the only to find fun in this game is to match up with the player who likes to have a good match but since this game is F2P and has children playing all unranked, Limited Time and ranked modes, it is [b] significantly hard to find one, [/b]

[h3] Online Play [/h3]
this one ruined my experience the most, if you are veteran player, i assume you are familiar with [b] "Phantom/Fake hits", [/b]  if not, this happens  when you predict the opponent and you hit them ...but the game doesn't register the hits, it changed their color and made a sound??
it happens really [i] often [/i] and miserable to experience first hand AND SOME THOSE HITS WON'T EVEN LAND ON THE OPPONENT??? Experimental mode made the game more fun to play and they removed it.. all the matches i've played is unfair and makes me want to quit then re-queue

[h3] what should they fix the game? [/h3]
everything, net code, weapons and legends balance and i understand it will take a while to make those changes but it's so bad

[h1] Should you play this game on all platforms even on PC? [/h1]
from the bottom of my heart, i would recommend this game but when you play the game. it's not really fun and ruined my mental stability fighting those kind of players, I WOULD NOT, NEVER, EVER RECOMMEND YOU PLAYING THIS ABSOLUTE TRASH GAME, it's really hard to choose words that is against my favourite 2D platform fighting game but it's too miserable to play right now and i wouldn't suggest you touching a dumb game even if you want to play 1-5 matches, the online play will totally ruin your experience... I WOULD recommend if you wanna play with friends and not take it seriously.

review:
TL;DR fun if you are highly, HIGHLY competitive and willing to grind hours without much care for aesthetics. Otherwise, you can find more fun elsewhere.

This game is not for the faint of heart. To put my opinion bluntly, it feels and plays like a highly competitive hellhole. Fun is derived not from playing it as a casual player, but playing it as a hardened gladiator. This games play like Super Smash Bros minus the lively animations that make the game appear friendly, and heavy emphasis on critical, sometimes pinpoint execution. (No joke, some combos only give you 1/2 frames to follow up and are very easy to mess up.)

Of course, that is not to say that it has no casual modes. It has plenty. You can hop into a custom game with a friend and play other modes like horde, bubble tag, temple climb, kung foot, dodge bomb, snow brawl - modes that do not put a heavy emphasis on competitive and moreso on goofiness. There are even custom lobbies out there for this exact purpose. However, there are definitely better games for a more casual experience than this one.

I strongly recommend it as it does fill its niche incredibly well: a high precision fighting platformer. I only got good after sinking an ungodly amount of time in this game, and even then I am far from the top. Understandably, this is not for everyone, and entering with the wrong mindset can cause more frustration than fun. Consider yourself warned.

P.S. To put into perspective, I never won a single 1 v 1 on my first day of playing this game. However... I have been winning quite consistently since.

review:
The game has several issues that has been present for several years.

The servers are absolute dogshit, meaning the game will randowmly freeze up mid-game or just kick you out. When your legend is still in the match the game is programmed to make it to dash for the ledge to die instantly. Every single game consists of FPS-drops, which is crucial to not happen since it's such a fast paced game. Some milliseconds might mean victory or defeat. It's just not acceptable to have FPS-drops in the game. It is completely beyond me that the devs haven't fixed this for all these years. Dodging where you should be able to dodge mostly doesn't register and some heavy attacks from some legends are stupid op like you could be standing outside of the attack's range but still get "sucked" into it for the animation's sake or something, I don't know.

New characters and weapons are added to the game. However, the most recent weapons added, like the battle boots and the chakram, are absolutely game breaking. Both of these weapons have too long-lasting light attacks, they cover an enormous amount of ground and it's strings are impossible to dodge. 

It just goes to show how little the devs care about making an actually good game. Been at it for years myself and I can say I have never had a pleasant experience with this game. You get a kick from winning matches and climbing in rating, but that's it. This game has never made me feel joy, it has always dragged me down into complete despair.

If you want to keep your sanity and your health, don't play this game.

review: This game is unbelievably amazing if your sole purpose in life is to have a sweaty, fat 12-year-old plow their scythe up your anal cavity and rip out all vital organs. I am starting to lose count of the amount of times I have been told to kill myself!! This game’s only made me break two monitors! Only two!! I am very appreciative of the experience Brawhalla has provided me, as it has excavated whole new emotions that I had yet to discover. review:
After playing this game for five years and over a thousand hours, I can say it could be much better. I don't know if the problem lies with the developer or Ubisoft, but the game has evolved very little. To this day, the game's ping is poor, the characters' hitboxes are inconsistent, and the training mode is extremely poorly designed. As a Tekken or Street Fighter player, I see a chasm in several basic aspects this game could have, but in five years, it hasn't evolved at all. There's also the fact that last year the price of coins for MTX went up; I, ​​who used to buy a skin or two almost every week, never bought anything again. As for the balancing, I wouldn't comment on it because it's crappy and poorly made.

My recommendation is: don't take this game seriously, because the company behind it doesn't take you seriously as a customer.

author: {'steamid': '76561198938341132', 'num_games_owned': 46, 'num_reviews': 3, 'playtime_forever': 133493, 'playtime_last_two_weeks': 0, 'playtime_at_review': 133388, 'last_played': 1760527377}
review:
[h1] Another Game trashed by Ubisoft [/h1]

I've have over 2k hours of experience, high elo, multiple accounts, and some tournaments under my belt. Would I recommend this game? [u] No. It's free and it's not worth it. [/u]

A game's learnability is based on the consistency of the game's experience. With that in mind, on paper this game is easier to pick-up with every character having two weapons as their form of attacks and only six unique moves (with possible variations on the move). 

This game would be fun for everyone but there's one consistent thing that makes the game inconsistent. The servers suck. They absolutely suck. This is one of the top free games out there and the servers in NA-E are horrible. There is latency issues, there is rubber-banding, and there is phantom sounds, etc. 

Now what they'll have you do if you report this is run a series of ping tests and send them the data (not useful at all, they know what they're doing wrong). I've had the pleasure of playing and testing this game on computers all over my region. Tell me why, on every stable internet connection I play on, there is a consistent latency loss in the servers here? Now to make sure I'm not spewing here, I tried connecting to EU, Asia, And Oceania servers. They all run with consistent ping that doesn't vary after multiple long tests more than 10ms. However when I play NA-E it spikes at least 1-2 times in 5 minutes (just pinging no game) with a 50-100 ms difference. Now 50-100 may not seem a lot but if you know fighting games it 100% does. You'll experience the rubber band effect where it snaps you back to what's actually happening in the game which is usually your death. 

Every update perpetuates this slow destruction of this game with servers getting worse and worse. All over a over-glorified flash game that should've invested in better servers ever since Covid-19 forced tournaments to be online. Somehow despite having rollback netcode the game just is worse when it comes to inputs and latency.

Look at the reviews, they reflect the game's state. If you're gonna start pedalling out $40 skins, you better start investing in fixing this problem. Because no one will be around to buy the next skin with the rate this game is sinking down the drain. 

Ubisoft hasn't made a good multiplayer experience in years. Well if solo player is your thing try not to ruin Assassin's Creed, oh wait. 

Seriously don't even install this game or any game owned/operated by Ubisoft. This game is a great couch play with friends. Easy to pick-up and has a skill-ceiling with a lot to master. Is it operated by a bunch of button-pushers? Yes. Should you play this as an online experience and spend money? NO.

review:
Gameplay-wise, it’s a 2D PvP Platform Fighting style of game similar to the Smash Ultimate series with tons of characters. There’s 100+ characters right now and there’s still more coming out. 
The gameplay is fun and replay-able and got me through most of COVID. It’s also really fun if you have friends to play with.

The only downsides in my experience of playing this game are:
- Players are toxic. This is the case whether they’re mechanically worse than you and spam Sigs (signature special moves) and win, whether it’s a close game where the two of you were actually evenly matched, or whether they’re better than you and you get stomped. Players are toxic and this adds to the frustration of losing in this game, though the player-base being full of shitters is no fault of the game. 
- There is no chat in public lobbies. There used to be one but it got removed because players wouldn’t stop using it for trash-talking. Only custom lobbies have a chat, but why use that when you’re probably already friends and on a Discord call together? 

TLDR: the gameplay is fun, especially if you have 1-7 friends to play with. Otherwise, prepare to hate this game and its player-base with every public game you play.

review:
I believe Brawlhalla is an excellent game. At its core, it is a 2D fighting game with simple graphics. Thanks to its visual style, it doesn’t require powerful hardware to run— even the weakest of computers can handle it.

The game offers a wide variety of combo possibilities, and it features a large roster of characters. The developers actively maintain the game by continuously releasing new fighters, each with their own unique style. While it is most enjoyable when played with friends, it can also be great fun with random players or even against AI opponents.

All in all, Brawlhalla is a very accessible game that remains enjoyable without spending a single cent.
